modes.principle: Exactly two modes exist. No third mode, no implicit hybrid, and no flag that blends them. The mode is determined before any check runs and is recorded in the report's environment block, because a reader cannot interpret a check's status without knowing which mode produced it.

modeSelection.rule: Project mode is entered when, and only when, doctor is invoked against a resolvable project root AND the invocation does not request core mode explicitly. Core mode is entered otherwise, including when a project root exists but is unresolvable. A project root that EXISTS but cannot be resolved (unreadable strict config, unreadable lock, corrupt or partially migrated state) does NOT downgrade doctor into core mode silently: doctor stays in the mode the invocation selected, reports the project-mode checks it could not reach as UNDETERMINED with a residual limitation, and says which resolution step failed.
modeSelection.whyNoSilentDowngrade: Silent downgrade is the failure this contract exists to prevent. A doctor that quietly becomes core mode on an unreadable lock returns a report whose checks all say the core install is fine - which is true and useless - while the reader's actual question (is this project's environment sound?) went unanswered and unmarked. The degraded-input behavior section makes this a testable property, not a preference.

coreMode.definition: Doctor with no project. It works without a project and reads only host-owned, install-scoped bytes: the installed generation's inventory, the core's own state, the component index/registry custody records, declared manifest metadata, host configuration layers 1, 2 and 5 (compiled defaults, user-global settings, allowlisted environment) as they resolve WITHOUT a project, last-known trust/revocation/expiry state as recorded on disk, and platform facts doctor can observe without a probe.
coreMode.worksWithoutAProject: Carried from C-2. Core mode never requires a project root, never searches upward for one, and never fails because none exists. Absence of a project is a NOT-APPLICABLE status on every project-scoped check, never a FAIL and never an UNDETERMINED.
readsWhat: installed generation inventory and its recorded digests
core-owned state (the Operational metadata class only)
component index custody records and admitted manifest metadata
user-global and compiled-default configuration layers, and the allowlisted environment layer
on-disk last-known revocation, metadata expiry, and anti-rollback state as VALUES ALREADY RECORDED - never refreshed
platform identity facts observable without executing anything (OS class, architecture)
doesNotDo: resolve or search for a project
read a project lock or tracked project intent
read the untracked local override layer (configuration layer 4)
write anything outside the Operational metadata class

mutate any byte outside the Operational metadata class - no lock is written, no cache rebuilt, no quarantine cleared, no trust state advanced, no migration moved in the prepare/commit/abort ladder (DP-4). The scope is definitional and is stated the same way at DP-1, DP-4, mechanism leg NA-3 and FC-RO's pass property; v1's unscoped 'mutate any byte' contradicted the bullet above it and the three scoped statements elsewhere.

projectMode.definition: Doctor with a project. It does everything core mode does, and additionally RESOLVES strict configuration and the project lock - and reports the resolution - without admitting analysis.

resolvesWhat.strictConfiguration: The effective configuration resolution defined by file 03's preserved V1 law, in its stated order: compiled defaults, user-global settings, tracked project intent, untracked local override, allowlisted environment, command flags. Doctor performs the SAME resolution the analysis path would perform - resolving a different one would make the report a report about a configuration nobody runs. Layer 4 obeys file 03 exactly: 'CI/non-interactive does not load or resolve layer 4 and does not reject merely because a layer-4 file exists', so doctor's layer-4 behavior follows the invocation's interactivity, and the report's environment block records which layer set was resolved so a reader never mistakes a local-interactive report for a CI one. CFG-9 is reported, not relaxed: doctor reports whether a non-allowlisted user-global key would enter analysis resolution, and that report is a check result, not permission for it to enter.
resolvesWhat.projectLock: The project component lock is READ and its recorded selections are reported: the selected signed index snapshot, component/artifact closure, platform alternative, subprotocol/state formats, and policy constraints it records. Doctor does not solve, re-solve, relax, or repair the lock, and no lock mutation can result from a doctor invocation - file 04's offline rule 'No missing payload triggers download, refresh, or lock mutation' is a hard bound on doctor as much as on update.

projectMode.reportsWhat: The resolution RESULT as evidence attached to checks: which layer won each analysis-affecting key (with file 03's decidingLayer provenance), which lock selections are present, which selections cannot be satisfied by the installed generation, and what is missing. Resolution provenance is data in a doctor check's evidence member; it is not a Plan input.
doesNotDo: negotiate or dispatch a provider role subprotocol
seal, write, or amend authoritative evidence

admittingAnalysis.whyThisNeedsAnExactDefinition: The entire read-only guarantee rests on this line. 'Project mode resolves strict config and lock without admitting analysis' is only a guarantee if 'admitting analysis' names a decidable set of acts; otherwise the clause is a mood. This contract therefore defines admission extensionally - as the six acts listed below - and then states the mechanism that prevents each, plus a negative-test class that fails if any occurs.
admittingAnalysis.definition: ADMITTING ANALYSIS is the act by which resolved project inputs become inputs to the semantic host's Snapshot/Plan/Run path. It has occurred if and only if at least one of the following six acts has occurred within the invocation:

acts.act: A Snapshot is constructed over project inputs.

A PlanId is minted or consumed, or any resolved value enters the existing Plan path (file 03: 'every analysis-affecting winning value and decidingLayer=4 provenance enters the existing Plan path' describes exactly the transition doctor must not perform).
A Run or Execution is opened.
A provider role subprotocol is negotiated or dispatched, i.e. any provider data-plane byte is exchanged.
A finding, fact, or Coverage value is produced.
Authoritative evidence is sealed, written, or amended.

admittingAnalysis.notAdmission: Reading project bytes is NOT admission. Resolving configuration is NOT admission. Reading and reporting the lock's recorded selections is NOT admission. Reporting that an analysis WOULD fail, or that a required component is absent, is NOT admission. The line is the transition into the host's semantic path, not the act of looking at a file.

preventionMechanism.statedHonestly: Four independent legs, of which exactly one is a live architectural rule, two ride candidate artifacts that bind nothing today, and one is a test. NONE of the four is measured enforcement in any shipping code. That is stated here rather than implied, because a mechanism claim that outruns its evidence is the failure this corpus rejects.

legs.leg: VALUE leg. Doctor's resolution produces a doctor-report resolution view - a value whose type is the report schema's evidence shape - and there is no conversion from it into any admission input. The semantic host exposes no entrypoint that consumes a doctor resolution view. Admission would require constructing an admission input from scratch, which is an act, not an omission.
legs.standing: Proposed here. Structural, checkable at blueprint time by the absence of such a conversion, and a negative test (FC-NC/FC-RO) fails if one exists.

legs.leg: PROTOCOL leg. When doctor probes a component under consent class CA-1, it uses control-plane functions F-2 (start/stop/supervise) and F-4 (health/resource/fault) ONLY. It never sends `select`. Without `selectAck` the provider data plane cannot lawfully carry a byte: the control-protocol candidate's RF-7 protocol-state-violation expressly covers 'data-plane bytes before selectAck (CH-DATA-EARLY)'. ADM-4 is therefore structurally unreachable through a doctor probe rather than merely unperformed.
legs.standing: Rides docs/coop/artifacts/control-protocol-contract.v2.json (c50a79fe...), status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING. The leg is exactly as strong as that candidate's eventual closure - see identityDependencies ID-DEP-4. It is cited as a candidate, never as applied authority.

legs.leg: STATE-CLASS leg. Doctor writes only the Operational metadata class, whose row in file 04's state-classes table names the 'Core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner' as sole writer and states the class is 'Excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly promotes a field'. Doctor promotes no field. Cross-class writes and cache-to-authority promotion are already negative tests under DR-124 and DR-G19, so this leg's violation is caught by an existing named gate rather than a new one.
legs.standing: Architecture prose in file 04 (measured), with the negative-test ownership at DR-124/DR-G19, both OPEN. Not enforcement today.

legs.leg: TEST leg. A negative-test class (FC-NC) that runs doctor in project mode over a project whose analysis would produce findings, and fails if the report contains any finding/fact/Coverage member, if any evidence record was written, if any Snapshot/Plan/Run/Execution identity was minted, or if a process/module trace shows a provider component was spawned or a data-plane byte moved. The trace evidence form is the one DR-G03 already names ('process/module trace') rather than a new evidence type.
legs.standing: Proposed requirement on the DR-G12 harness's retained evidence. No fixture exists.

preventionMechanism.residualLimitation: With NA-2 riding a candidate and NA-3 riding open rows, the non-admission property is today argued structurally and tested negatively; it is not enforced by any measured mechanism. A reviewer should read this as a design that makes admission an affirmative act requiring code that does not exist, not as a claim that admission is impossible.

admittingAnalysis.identityMintingBound: Doctor mints NO identity of any kind - no Snapshot, Plan, Run, or Execution identity, and no derived digest over doctor's own report. This is doubly bound: ADM-1 through ADM-3 forbid it, and the derivation recipes for those identities are parked at DR-006, so minting one would also be inventing a parked recipe. The doctor report is consequently not an identity-bearing artifact, which is why its environment block may carry a wall-clock timestamp without any identity consequence.

stableMachineSchema.scopeOfThisSection: The STRUCTURE of the doctor report and the rules that make it stable for a machine reader. It does not enumerate the product's slice-1 check catalog: which concrete checks exist is blueprint work under D-002's slice, and inventing a catalog here would decide product scope from a schema artifact. What is bound is the shape a check occupies, the closed status set, the evidence and residual-limitation obligations, the environment block, and the stability rules.
stableMachineSchema.identifierDiscipline: Every identifier this section introduces (the status tokens, the check-class names, the outcome-class ids elsewhere) is a SURFACE-LOCAL identity of the doctor report schema, in the same sense the control-protocol candidate's RF-1..RF-8 are surface-local to that plane. None is a D9 code, an exit code, a fate, a permission token, or a fault cause, and none maps to any of those by this artifact.

members.name: schemaVersion
members.semantics: The version of THIS report schema and nothing else. It is not the core version, not a component version, not the control-protocol version, and not a bundle version. File 04's separate-matrices section is explicit that 'There is no shared N/N-1/N-2 promise and no common version number'; this member exists so the doctor report never borrows one.

members.name: mode
members.semantics: Which of the two modes produced this report. Carried in the envelope AND in environment so a reader that consumes only the envelope cannot misread a core-mode report as a project verdict.

members.name: outcome
members.type: one of the outcome-class identifiers bound at outcomeStructure
members.semantics: The report's single overall outcome class. Structure only; the D9/exit VALUE it maps to is DR-007's (ID-DEP-1).

members.name: environment
members.semantics: See environmentBlock.

members.name: checks
members.semantics: Every check doctor considered in this invocation, INCLUDING those it did not run. A check doctor decided not to run appears with status NOT-APPLICABLE or CONSENT-REQUIRED; it is never omitted. Omission and non-execution must be distinguishable, and omission is not available as a way to express non-execution.

members.name: consentRecords
members.semantics: One record per consented action ATTEMPTED in this invocation, empty in the default posture. See consentModel.mandatoryPostReport for the record shape.

members.name: residualLimitations
members.semantics: Report-level limitations that belong to no single check - for example 'last-known revocation state is N days stale and no network consent was named'. Per-check limitations live on the check.

reportEnvelope.whatIsNotInTheEnvelope: No aggregate boolean. There is deliberately no top-level `ready`, `healthy`, or `ok` member. A single boolean is the shape that makes a partial report read as a clean bill, and it is the prototype behavior DIFF-4 rejects. The overall outcome class carries the summary, and the outcome classes are constructed so that 'could not determine' is not spelled the same way as 'determined to be fine'.

members.name: id
members.type: string, a surface-local stable check identifier
members.semantics: Stable across schema versions. A check id, once published, names that check forever; retiring a check means marking it retired, never reusing the id for a different question.

members.name: class
members.type: one of the check classes below
members.semantics: The structural category the check belongs to. Classes exist so degraded-input behavior can be stated per class rather than per unnamed check, and so a reader can interpret an unknown check id.

members.name: status
members.type: one of the five status tokens below

members.name: title
members.semantics: Human-readable question the check answers. Bounded and redaction-classified like every other string member.

members.name: evidence
members.semantics: What doctor actually observed, in machine form. See evidenceItem. Evidence is required to be present for PASS and FAIL: a verdict with no evidence is a claim, and this corpus does not accept claims without measured bases.

members.name: residualLimitation
members.semantics: REQUIRED MEMBER, nullable value. It must be non-null whenever status is UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED, and whenever a PASS or FAIL rests on evidence with a stated bound narrower than the check's title implies. Making the member required-but-nullable rather than optional means a producer must decide about it, and a reader can tell 'no limitation' from 'nobody considered it' only if the member is always present.

members.name: remediation
members.semantics: Present when doctor can name an operator action. Never executable, never applied by doctor. See doctorRemediationRecord.

tokens.meaning: The check ran and the property held.
The check ran and the property did not hold. This is a statement about the ENVIRONMENT, not about doctor.

The check could not reach a verdict: an input was unreadable, a dependency was absent, or an observation was bounded out. This is a statement about DOCTOR's reach, not about the environment. residualLimitation must be non-null and must say what blocked the verdict.
The check does not apply in this mode or on this platform - for example a project-scoped check in core mode. Applicability is a property of the invocation, decided before the check runs.
tokens.note: Success-bearing because an inapplicable check is not a defect; but it is distinguishable from PASS, so an aggregate that counted NOT-APPLICABLE as evidence of health would be visibly wrong.

tokens.meaning: The check exists and applies, but its evidence needs one of the four consented action classes and no consent was named. This is the honest name for 'we did not look'.
tokens.note: Deliberately NOT called SKIPPED. 'Skipped' invites a reader to treat the check as immaterial; CONSENT-REQUIRED states that the answer is unknown and names what would obtain it.

statusTokens.theHonestyRule: UNDETERMINED and CONSENT-REQUIRED are NOT success-bearing. A check nobody could answer must never aggregate as though it passed. This single rule is what stops a doctor report from becoming a clean bill of health for an environment nobody managed to inspect, and it is the rule the outcome classes and the fixture classes both test.

checkClasses.name: INSTALL-INTEGRITY
checkClasses.scope: The installed generation's own bytes, inventory, and recorded digests.

checkClasses.name: TRUST-STATE
checkClasses.scope: On-disk trust roots, last-known revocation, metadata expiry, anti-rollback counters - as RECORDED, never refreshed.

checkClasses.name: COMPONENT-INVENTORY
checkClasses.scope: Admitted component index custody records, declared manifest metadata, admission status, deprecation/alias-window state.

checkClasses.name: CONFIGURATION-RESOLUTION
checkClasses.scope: The resolved configuration and its provenance, including CFG-9 reporting.
checkClasses.modes: project (NOT-APPLICABLE in core mode for project layers; the user-global and default layers are reportable in core mode)

checkClasses.name: LOCK-STATE
checkClasses.scope: The project lock's recorded selections and whether the installed generation can satisfy them.

checkClasses.name: STATE-CLASS-HEALTH
checkClasses.scope: The Operational metadata and rebuildable cache/index classes doctor is permitted to observe - presence, readability, migration state.

checkClasses.name: PLATFORM-PREREQUISITE
checkClasses.scope: Platform facts and declared external-system prerequisites, including the DR-119/D-008 customer-owned external-system exception that 'appears in manifest and doctor output'.

checkClasses.name: COMPONENT-LIVENESS
checkClasses.scope: Whether an admitted component actually starts and reports health. ALWAYS consent class CA-1; in the default posture every check in this class reports CONSENT-REQUIRED.

evidenceItem.principle: Evidence is what doctor OBSERVED, expressed so a reader can tell observation from inference. Every item carries its own bound.

members.name: kind
members.semantics: What sort of observation this is: a recorded digest read from custody, a declared manifest field, a resolved configuration value with its deciding layer, a filesystem presence/readability fact, a platform fact, or a consented-action result.

members.name: observed
members.semantics: The observation, redaction-classified per redaction.defaultRedactedClasses before it enters the report.

members.name: bound
members.semantics: What this observation does and does not establish - the bound is the claim. An evidence item whose bound is unstated cannot support a PASS.

members.name: provenance
members.semantics: Where the observation came from: the custody record, the configuration layer, the manifest field, or the consent record id for a consented action.

evidenceItem.whatEvidenceMayNotBe: Evidence may never be a raw byte dump, an unbounded string, an untruncated stderr tail, a raw error object, or a secret value in any form including a prefix preview. The prototype's Error-object deny-by-default (toSafeDiagnosticData returns name + scrubbed message + the literal note 'error-object-redacted') is carried forward as the correct posture.

members.name: statement
members.semantics: What was NOT established, in the reader's terms.

members.name: cause
members.semantics: Why: input-unreadable, dependency-absent, consent-not-named, observation-bounded, offline-staleness, mode-scope, or source-changed-under-observation. A closed set at this surface; it is not a fault cause and does not map to D9's observation->faultCause gap, which is DR-007's (ID-DEP-1). The seventh cause carries DEG-7: a source whose identity changed between doctor's first and last measurement of it, which withdraws every verdict that rested on that source. Adding a cause category is expressly additive-safe under this schema's own stability rules (stabilityRules.mayBeAddedWithoutBreakingAReader), and readers must tolerate an unknown cause.

members.name: wouldBeResolvedBy
members.semantics: The operator or policy act that would let the check reach a verdict, or null when nothing available to the operator would. Null is a legitimate and important value: some limitations are structural.

environmentBlock.principle: Enough for a reader to interpret the checks, and nothing more. Every member is redaction-classified; the block is a common leak site precisely because it feels like harmless context.

members.name: modeSelectionReason
members.semantics: Why this mode - including 'project root present but unresolvable', which is the case a reader most needs to see.

members.name: installedGenerationRef
members.type: reference to the installed generation's recorded identity
members.semantics: A REFERENCE to an identity the lifecycle surface already records, never an identity minted here.

members.name: platform
members.semantics: The coarse platform facts D-002's four supported platforms are expressed in. Not a hostname, not a username, not a machine identifier.

members.name: configurationLayersResolved
members.semantics: Which of file 03's six layers were resolved in this invocation - the member that lets a reader tell a CI report from a local-interactive one, since layer 4 differs between them by file 03's law.

members.name: offlinePosture
members.semantics: Whether any egress consent was named in this invocation, and the recorded age of the last-known revocation and metadata expiry state. Staleness is a fact doctor reports; refreshing it is not doctor's act.

members.name: generatedAt
members.semantics: Wall clock. Carries no identity consequence because doctor mints no identity (modes.admittingAnalysis.identityMintingBound).

members.name: projectRootRef
members.semantics: Never a raw absolute path, in EITHER mode. Paths inside the project root are project-relative; anything outside collapses to a non-identifying marker. This rule is STRICTER than the prototype's projectRelativePath, whose no-projectRoot branch returns the full absolute path scrubbed and bounded at 512 characters rather than collapsed (DIFF-10) - and that branch is exactly the core-mode case, where no project root exists. In core mode this member is null, and no absolute path reaches the report by any other member either: environmentBlock.expresslyExcluded names the absolute install path, the username and the home-directory path.

expresslyExcluded: environment variable VALUES (presence only, and only for variables a manifest declares - see DIFF-7)

mayBeAddedWithoutBreakingAReader: A new check id, in any existing check class. Readers must tolerate unknown check ids and must interpret them by their class and status alone.
A new check CLASS, provided existing classes keep their meaning. A reader that does not know a class treats its checks by status only.
A new OPTIONAL member on the check object, the evidence item, the environment block, or a consent record.
A new evidence kind, a new residual-limitation cause category, or a new consent-record member, all of which readers must tolerate as unknown.
A new entry in an array-valued member.
mayNeverChange: The five status tokens: no token may be removed, renamed, or repurposed, and no sixth token may be added. Adding a status token silently repartitions every existing reader's success/non-success arithmetic. A new distinction must be expressed in a new optional member, never in the status set.

The success-bearing partition of the five tokens. PASS and NOT-APPLICABLE are success-bearing; FAIL, UNDETERMINED and CONSENT-REQUIRED are not. Moving a token across this line changes what every published report meant.
The meaning of any published check id.

The presence-requirement of any required member, including the required-but-nullable residualLimitation. Making a required member optional breaks readers that rely on its presence to distinguish 'considered and none' from 'not considered'.
The type of any published member.
The rule that non-executed checks appear with a status rather than being omitted.
The rule that the envelope carries no aggregate boolean.
stabilityRules.breakingChangeHandling: Any change in the may-never-change list is a new schemaVersion major, and a reader of an unsupported major REFUSES rather than best-effort parsing - the same posture the control-protocol candidate takes at RF-1 for an unsupported control major. A doctor report from an unsupported future major is not partially interpreted.
readerObligations: Never infer PASS from the absence of a member or a check.
Never aggregate UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED as success.
Refuse an unsupported schemaVersion major rather than parse it.

compatibilityMatrixRow.assertion: The doctor report schema owns its OWN DR-111 compatibility-matrix row and never shares a version number with any other surface - file 04: 'There is no shared N/N-1/N-2 promise and no common version number.'
compatibilityMatrixRow.measuredCaveat: File 04's separate-matrices section enumerates eight surfaces (distribution core and core state; signed root/index/manifest/lock schemas; common control protocol; TypeScript provider protocol major 1; Rust merged provider protocol major 2; each other component role API/subprotocol; component-owned state schema; evidence/custody/replay formats) and a machine-OUTPUT schema is not among them. This artifact does not add a row to DR-111 by assertion; it proposes the row's content and records the enumeration gap as a tension (tensionsObserved T-4) for DR-111 and the coordinator to resolve. Admitting the row is DR-111's act.

proposedRowContent.note: The six cells file 04 requires of every matrix: 'Each matrix declares current writer, supported readers, migrations/bridges, future-major refusal, downgrade/no-return, and test evidence.'
proposedRowContent.currentWriter: doctorReportSchemaVersion 1 - the host, sole writer. No component writes a doctor report; a component's contribution enters as evidence inside a host-written check.
proposedRowContent.supportedReaders: Major 1 exactly. No cross-major window exists yet and none can exist before a second major does.
proposedRowContent.migrationsAndBridges: None. A doctor report is a produced-and-consumed document, not durable state; there is nothing to migrate. A future major is produced or not produced, never bridged.
proposedRowContent.futureMajorRefusal: Typed refusal on an unsupported major, never best-effort parse (stabilityRules.breakingChangeHandling).
proposedRowContent.downgradeAndNoReturn: Not applicable in the state sense - no durable state carries this schema. A host that can emit only major N cannot emit major N-1 on request; the invocation refuses rather than emitting a downgraded shape whose fidelity it cannot state.
proposedRowContent.testEvidence: FC-SCHEMA's fixture classes, retained under DR-G12.

compatibilityMatrixRow.ridesOn: DR-111 (OPEN). Window SEMANTICS and the matrix's evidence cells are DR-111's to define - identityDependencies ID-DEP-3.

defaultPosture.verbatimSource: Doctor defaults to read-only, no component code, no network, and no mutation.

fourDefaultProperties.meaning: Doctor reads; it does not write. The one exception is the Operational metadata class doctor is the declared owner of (file 04's state table), and even there doctor writes only its own audit/journal record of having run - never a byte another surface reads as authority.
fourDefaultProperties.departureBy: No consent class departs from this. There is no consented doctor mutation. A doctor that could be consented into mutating is a repair tool, and repair is DR-110's surface, not this one.

fourDefaultProperties.meaning: No component executable is spawned and no component code path runs in-process.

Doctor opens no socket, sends no byte, and resolves no name. Last-known revocation, metadata expiry, and index state are read as RECORDED values; file 04's 'No missing payload triggers download, refresh, or lock mutation' binds doctor at full width.
No byte outside the Operational metadata class changes. No lock is written, no cache is rebuilt, no migration is prepared or committed, no quarantine is cleared, no trust state is advanced.
fourDefaultProperties.departureBy: No consent class departs from this - as DP-1.

defaultPosture.twoOfFourAreAbsolute: DP-1 and DP-4 have NO consented departure. Only DP-2 and DP-3 are consentable, plus the two action classes that are neither strictly component code nor strictly network (CA-2 customer tool execution, CA-3 probe). This asymmetry is deliberate and is the strongest single property in this contract: doctor is the surface users reach when things are broken, and a diagnostic that can be talked into changing the thing it is diagnosing destroys the evidence it exists to produce.
defaultPosture.everyDepartureIsNamed: In the default posture, checks whose evidence would require any of the four action classes report CONSENT-REQUIRED. There is no silent degradation to a weaker check, no probe-if-available heuristic, and no environment-sniffing that turns a probe on because it looks safe.

consentableActionClasses.name: component tool execution
consentableActionClasses.covers: Spawning an admitted component's executable, or running component code in-process, in order to obtain a check's evidence - the COMPONENT-LIVENESS check class.
consentableActionClasses.scopeBound: Bound to: the exact doctor invocation; the named check ids the consent serves; the exact component generation identity and its admitted manifest digest (the custody join the manifest candidate already records - this is file 03's 'exact component bytes'); and the PLATFORM the consent is given on. It expires with the invocation and is never persisted by doctor as standing consent. Carried ALONGSIDE the consent but NOT as authorization parameters: a doctor-side observation deadline and a bound on bytes doctor will accept from the component - see boundsAreNotPermissionParameters. PLATFORM is added in v2 because file 03 lines 101-103 require trusted-code fallback consent to be 'bound to exact component bytes, operation, scope, and platform', CA-1 IS trusted-code fallback by this contract's own honestBound, and v1 bound three of the four.
consentableActionClasses.protocolShape: Control-plane F-2 (hello/helloAck, ping/pong, shutdown/shutdownAck) and F-4 (health/healthReport, resourceReport, fault) ONLY. `select` is never sent, so the provider data plane never opens (modes.admittingAnalysis.preventionMechanism NA-2). `effectRequest` is never sent either: doctor brokers no effect and does not become an effect broker because it happened to open a channel (controlProtocolAlignment.functionsDoctorNeverUses). Refusals doctor encounters on the channel use the control plane's RF-1..RF-8 families as-is; doctor mints no refusal family of its own. TWO CONSEQUENCES OF THE NO-BROKER POSTURE, recorded rather than left to be discovered: (1) DR-105's only token whose cells carry ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER is the brokered-effect token, so a doctor that never opens a brokered request reaches NO enforced cell in that candidate's table by any action - consent in the joined design would be purely disclosive. This contract judges the broker backwards for doctor's probes, which are host-initiated rather than component-initiated, and records the consequence instead of the alternative. (2) This contract's CONSENT-REQUIRED is a CHECK STATUS, not a refusal family: it is emitted when no consent was named, before any channel exists, so it reaches no RF-6 and is not doctor minting a refusal. Whether it is the same decision as DR-105's own consent-required-and-unavailable refusal family - which that candidate defines as refining RF-6 - is a join question the routed actor decision reaches, not a mapping this contract may assert.
consentableActionClasses.honestBound: Executing a first-party or explicitly-trusted component is executing trusted code in the TCB. File 03: 'A child process is fault containment, not a sandbox.' The consent authorizes the execution; it does not contain it, and the post-report must say so.

consentableActionClasses.name: customer tool execution
consentableActionClasses.covers: Executing a customer-owned external tool or platform facility - the DR-119/D-008 narrow exception case, which file 02 requires to appear 'in manifest and doctor output' with 'typed absence/failure behavior'.
consentableActionClasses.scopeBound: Bound to: the exact invocation; the named checks; the exact DECLARED external-system identity from the manifest (never a name doctor constructed and never an ambient PATH resolution - see DIFF-13); and the PLATFORM the consent is given on. Carried ALONGSIDE the consent but NOT as authorization parameters: a doctor-side observation deadline, an output byte bound, and the descriptor-controlled argument vector, which is DISCLOSED in the post-report rather than scoped by the consent - v1 bound the consent to 'the exact argument vector', which is the argument-level policy surface DR-105 reserved to DR-125 under another word, and that binding is withdrawn (boundsAreNotPermissionParameters).
consentableActionClasses.honestBound: A customer-owned tool is outside OpenSIP's signed closure entirely. Doctor cannot state what it reads, writes, or sends. Consenting to CA-2 is consenting to run a program whose behavior OpenSIP does not bound, and the post-report says exactly that as a residual limitation, every time, without exception.

consentableActionClasses.name: probes
consentableActionClasses.covers: An observation that reaches beyond reading host-owned bytes but executes no component or customer code: stat-ing or reading a path outside the install and project roots, opening a local socket or named pipe, reading an OS keychain entry, or querying a privileged platform facility.
consentableActionClasses.scopeBound: Bound to: the exact invocation; the named checks; an explicit enumeration of the exact resources the probe may touch - probe consent is never open-ended, and 'probe the system' is not a grantable scope; and the PLATFORM the consent is given on, which for this class is load-bearing rather than formal, since a keychain, a named pipe and a privileged platform facility are different objects on each supported platform. Carried alongside but not as an authorization parameter: a doctor-side observation deadline (boundsAreNotPermissionParameters).
consentableActionClasses.honestBound: A probe is an observation, but observations are not free: reading a keychain entry may prompt the operator's OS, and stat-ing a path discloses that OpenSIP looked. The post-report names the exact resources touched.

consentableActionClasses.name: egress
consentableActionClasses.covers: Any network send or receive by doctor - refreshing revocation state, reaching an index, or contacting a declared external service.
consentableActionClasses.scopeBound: Bound to: the exact invocation; the named checks; the exact endpoint or endpoint set, enumerated and never a pattern; and the PLATFORM the consent is given on. Carried alongside but not as authorization parameters: a doctor-side observation deadline and a byte bound in both directions, whose actual counts are DISCLOSED afterwards under file 04's own 'endpoint/bytes where relevant' obligation (boundsAreNotPermissionParameters).
consentableActionClasses.honestBound: Egress discloses to the far side that this installation exists and what it asked. The post-report carries endpoint and bytes in both directions - which is precisely why file 04's post-report clause says 'endpoint/bytes where relevant'.

consentDoesNotCascade.rule: Consent to one action class is NEVER consent to another, and consent to execute something is never consent for what that thing then does. Concretely: CA-1 consent does not authorize the component's egress; CA-2 consent does not authorize the customer tool's egress or its filesystem writes; CA-3 consent to read a keychain entry does not authorize reading a second one.
consentDoesNotCascade.theHardCase: A component or customer tool whose DECLARED posture is networked or auth-required. Doctor cannot prevent an executed program from sending a packet - file 03's confinement honesty and the prototype's own ADR-0092 ('The declaration is honest labeling, not a sandbox'; 'requires stays declaration-only') both say so. Therefore: consenting to CA-1 or CA-2 for a target whose declared posture includes network REQUIRES a separately named CA-4 consent, and if CA-4 is absent the action is REFUSED rather than executed-and-hoped. Where the target's posture is declared local-only, doctor executes under CA-1/CA-2 alone and the post-report records, as a residual limitation, that the no-egress property is DECLARED and not enforced by doctor.
consentDoesNotCascade.whyRefuseRatherThanWarn: Deny wins; absence denies (file 03). A warning that the executed tool might egress, attached to a report produced after it already ran, is not a consent model - it is a notification. The refusal is the only form in which the default posture survives contact with a networked target.

howConsentIsNamed.principle: Consent is NAMED, meaning it identifies the action class and its scope explicitly at the invocation or in pre-existing policy. It is never inferred from a flag that means something else, never implied by the presence of a credential, and never obtained by prompting in a non-interactive context.

twoAdmissibleCarriers.rule: The operator names the action class and the scope on the invocation. The naming is per class - there is no all-classes token, because a single token that turns on component execution, customer execution, probes and egress together is the opposite of named consent.

A configuration-resolved policy that names the classes and scopes permitted in this project or for this operator. This is the ONLY carrier available in CI: file 03 is exact that 'CI never prompts and needs pre-existing policy', and doctor inherits that rule without amendment.

expresslyNotAdmissible: prompting in a non-interactive or CI context
inferring consent from the presence of a credential environment variable
inferring consent from a declared network posture
a component or manifest granting itself the consent - file 03: 'A manifest, repository, or publisher cannot grant authority to itself'
an all-classes or wildcard consent token
consent persisted by doctor from a previous invocation

dr105Join.problemStated: Consent must ride DR-105's permission vocabulary rather than minting a second one. DR-105's ROW is OPEN, measured at the file 08 digest. A DR-105 candidate was being authored in a parallel lane during this authoring: none existed when this artifact's inputs were measured, and one (permission-truth-tables.v1.json, 0f73f31c..., CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW / binds NOTHING) appeared before finalization - recorded at recordedInputs.lateMeasurementObservation as OBSERVED, NOT CONSUMED. Either way the position is the same, and that is the point of designing the join this way: the join activates on the ROW's closure, not on a candidate's existence. This contract names the dependency in symmetry-clause form, DEFINES THE JOIN, and mints no token.
whatThisContractDefines: The four action classes CA-1..CA-4 as DOCTOR-SIDE, SURFACE-LOCAL action-class identities - the same status the control-protocol candidate's RF-* families hold on their plane. They are carriers, not permissions.

The requirement that each action class resolve to DR-105 permission token(s) before it can be exercised: an action class with no resolved token is UNEXERCISABLE, and every check depending on it reports CONSENT-REQUIRED with cause consent-not-named.

The record shape that carries the resolution result (consentRecord.permissionRef below), as a RESERVED BINDING POINT in the idiom the component-manifest candidate already uses for exactly this dependency at its ID-DEP-11.

The two records every consent carries, taken verbatim from file 03's existing vocabulary rather than invented here: authorization ('requested', then resolved to 'granted' or 'denied') and execution ('enforced', 'disclosed-trusted-code', or 'refused').

The laws that hold regardless of which tokens DR-105 mints - SIX, not five: deny wins; absence denies; a manifest/repository/publisher cannot grant authority to itself; required confinement refuses when unenforceable; CI never prompts and needs pre-existing policy; AND - added in v2, having been omitted from v1's enumeration of five - 'Trusted-code fallback requires explicit consent bound to exact component bytes, operation, scope, and platform' (file 03 lines 101-103, quoted whole at the digest recorded in recordedInputs). That sixth law is the file-03 law most directly governing this contract's own subject, and v1 omitted the one its four scope bounds most needed to carry: none of them bound PLATFORM. All four now do. NOTE ON WIDTH: the source bounds this law to TRUSTED-CODE FALLBACK, which is exactly what CA-1 is; the DR-105 candidate's PR-7 reads it wider, to cover a consented probe or egress as well. That widening is DR-105's and is not adopted here as file 03's - CA-2, CA-3 and CA-4 bind platform because a consent that does not name the platform cannot be evaluated against a per-platform truth table under any reading, not because this contract has decided how wide file 03's sentence reaches.
whatThisContractDoesNotDefine: the per-platform truth table for any effect

the grant-revocation linearization semantics - the ordering of acceptance, effect-commit, revocation, cleanup and audit against a durable monotonic sequence. WHAT THIS CONTRACT NO LONGER DEFERS: the prior question of what a doctor consent IS as a doctor-side object, which v1 left to DR-105 while DR-105 left it to DR-114's owner - a circular deferral an independent coherence review measured on both sides. Stated plainly here: a doctor consent is NAMED by the operator at the invocation or by pre-existing policy, is bound to that single invocation, is carried in memory for its duration, is reported in the mandatory post-report, and is NEVER persisted, journaled, sequenced or carried into a later invocation. Doctor writes no journal, holds no sequence numbers, and mints no identity (ID-DEP-10). Whether that object ALSO constitutes a grant in DR-105's permission journal - and is therefore revocable, expiring and linearized like any other - is NOT a fact about doctor that doctor was withholding; it is the routed ACTOR decision (actorMismatch, ID-DEP-12), and it is named there with its decider rather than passed back.
whether a given action class maps to one token or several

theJoinExactly.shapeUntilDr105Closes: RESERVED BINDING POINT: { reserved: true, ridesOn: ['DR-105'] }
theJoinExactly.activationRule: The member activates on DR-105's closure. Populating it before then is a schema violation in the same class as the component-manifest candidate's RJ-6/RESERVED_FIELD_POPULATED, cited at digest as that candidate's rule and not re-minted here.
theJoinExactly.cardinalityIsDr105s: Whether an action class maps to exactly one DR-105 token, to several, or to a token plus a scope expression is DR-105's to decide. This contract fixes UNCONDITIONALLY that the mapping is FAIL-CLOSED: an unmapped class is unexercisable, never permitted-by-default. It no longer fixes that the mapping is TOTAL over the four classes. v1 asserted totality unconditionally; an independent coherence review measured that, under one of the two readings the pair admits, totality is unsatisfiable IN PRINCIPLE rather than pending DR-105's closure - because if host-surface actions are outside the component permission vocabulary, then CA-1..CA-4 are outside it too and no closure of DR-105 can ever satisfy the requirement. Totality is therefore CONDITIONAL on the routed actor decision (actorMismatch): it is a coherent requirement only under a disposition that brings host-surface actions inside the vocabulary. Where a class carries a host actor and the disposition leaves host actors outside, that class's authorization origin is the UNOWNED surface named at ID-DEP-12 - not a token this contract may mint, and not a reason the class becomes permitted by default.
theJoinExactly.directionOfAuthority: DR-105 owns the vocabulary; doctor owns the action classes that quantify over it. If DR-105's closure names an effect class doctor does not exercise, doctor gains nothing; if doctor later needs an action class DR-105's vocabulary cannot express, that is a DR-105 successor's problem, not a licence for doctor to mint a token.
theJoinExactly.symmetryClause: If DR-105 closes by scoped disposition rather than a binding permission vocabulary, doctor's consented action classes ship reduced, re-scoped, or wait, by that disposition's terms - and the reduced form is the DEFAULT POSTURE, which is fully specified here and needs no token at all. Doctor without any consented action class is a complete, useful, and honest product; it simply reports CONSENT-REQUIRED for the COMPONENT-LIVENESS class and for every check needing a probe or egress. None of this survives on prose.

dr105Join.d002AlreadyScopedThis: D-002's condition-2 row set records DR-105 as 'scoped to the permissions the slice actually exercises: local read/write + consented doctor probes'. The join defined here is the doctor half of that already-recorded scoping, not a new ask.

mandatoryPostReport.verbatimObligation: Every consented action reports scope, endpoint/bytes where relevant, result, and residual limitation.
mandatoryPostReport.rule: One consent record per consented action ATTEMPTED - including actions that were consented and then refused, failed, timed out, or were bounded out. A consented action that produced nothing still produces a record. Absence of a record means the action was never attempted; it never means the action produced nothing worth saying. AND: absence of a record never means the action's OUTCOME was nothing. Where doctor initiated an effect and cannot state whether it landed, the record is written with the reserved effectOutcome member unpopulated and a non-null residual limitation saying so - never omitted, and never recorded as a refusal.

recordMembers.name: id
recordMembers.semantics: Surface-local record id, referenced by the evidence items it produced.

recordMembers.name: permissionRef
recordMembers.semantics: RESERVED BINDING POINT ({ reserved: true, ridesOn: ['DR-105'] }) - the DR-105 join above.

recordMembers.name: scope
recordMembers.semantics: OBLIGATION 'scope', verbatim. The exact bound the consent carried: which checks, which target identity (component generation + admitted manifest digest, or declared external-system identity), which enumerated resources, which deadline, which byte cap.

recordMembers.name: endpoint
recordMembers.semantics: OBLIGATION 'endpoint ... where relevant'. Non-null for CA-4 (the exact endpoint contacted) and for CA-3 where the probe targeted a named resource. Null with an explicit reason for classes where it does not apply - required-but-nullable so a reader can tell 'no endpoint' from 'nobody recorded one'.

recordMembers.name: bytes
recordMembers.semantics: OBLIGATION 'bytes where relevant'. For CA-4: bytes sent and bytes received, separately. For CA-1/CA-2: bytes accepted from the target's output. Null with a reason where not applicable.

recordMembers.name: authorization
recordMembers.semantics: File 03's first record, verbatim vocabulary: 'requested', then resolved to 'granted' or 'denied'.

recordMembers.name: execution
recordMembers.semantics: File 03's second record, verbatim vocabulary: 'enforced', 'disclosed-trusted-code', or 'refused'. For CA-1 and CA-2 against a first-party or explicitly-trusted target with no measured confinement, the honest value is 'disclosed-trusted-code' - and recording 'enforced' without measured confinement would be exactly the claim file 03's confinement-honesty section forbids.
recordMembers.thisMemberIsAboutCONFINEMENT_NOT_OUTCOME: Stated in v2 because an independent coherence review measured the conflation as the pair's sharpest single defect. These three values answer 'was the act contained, and by what'. They do NOT answer 'did the effect happen'. In particular: 'refused' means DOCTOR DID NOT PERFORM THE ACT, and it may NEVER be written for an act doctor initiated whose outcome doctor does not know. Writing 'refused' for an unknown outcome would let a summary count the effect among the ones that did not happen, which is false and is the mismodeling the DR-105 candidate expressly forbids in its own notRefusals section. The outcome lives at `effectOutcome` below, and it is not carried in prose in `result` either - narrating an unknown outcome in free text is the narration this corpus's honesty discipline exists to stop.

recordMembers.name: result
recordMembers.semantics: OBLIGATION 'result', verbatim. What the action produced, bounded and redaction-classified.

recordMembers.name: residualLimitation
recordMembers.semantics: OBLIGATION 'residual limitation', verbatim. NON-NULLABLE on a consent record - unlike on a check. Every consented action has a residual limitation, because every consented action departs from a default the contract otherwise guarantees, and the thing given up is always statable. For CA-2 it always includes that the customer tool's behavior is unbounded by OpenSIP; for CA-1/CA-2 against a declared local-only target it always includes that the no-egress property is declared and not enforced.

recordMembers.name: effectOutcome
recordMembers.shapeUntilTheActorDecisionAndDr105Close: RESERVED BINDING POINT: { reserved: true, ridesOn: ['DR-105'], conditionedOn: 'the ACTOR decision at ID-DEP-12' }
recordMembers.semantics: WHAT HAPPENED to the effect the consented action initiated, as distinct from whether the act was authorized (`authorization`), whether it was contained (`execution`), and what it produced (`result`). This member exists because v1 had NO carrier for it and an independent coherence review demonstrated that every value then available was wrong for the same case: a consented CA-4 egress that crashed between initiating the send and observing the result cannot honestly be called 'refused' (bytes may have left the host), 'enforced' (a statement about confinement, and one this contract's own FC-CONSENT fails on), or 'disclosed-trusted-code' (also about confinement). The same hole swallows an effect that completed before a revocation landed.
recordMembers.whyTheValueVocabularyIsNotMintedHere: The values that belong in this member are the DR-105 candidate's own - it defines them as first-class OUTCOMES that must be disclosed and must not be modeled as refusals. Minting doctor-side synonyms would be exactly the semantic duplication this contract is otherwise careful to avoid, and would produce two vocabularies for one fact.
recordMembers.whyItIsNotAStatusToken: The five check status tokens are CLOSED and may never gain a sixth (stabilityRules.mayNeverChange), and rightly: a status describes a CHECK's reach, and adding a token silently repartitions every reader's success arithmetic. An effect outcome is a property of a consented ACTION, not of a check, so it belongs on the consent record. The status set is untouched by this member, and this contract's UNDETERMINED remains a statement about doctor's reach that must never be used to carry an unknown effect outcome (sharedTermDisambiguation).
recordMembers.untilItActivates: The member is present and reserved. A consented action whose effect outcome doctor cannot state is NOT recorded as refused, enforced, or narrated away: the consent record carries the reserved member unpopulated and a NON-NULL residual limitation saying in terms that doctor initiated the effect and cannot state whether it landed. That is a stated bound rather than a silent mismodeling, and it is the honest thing this contract can say before the actor decision is made.
recordMembers.schemaStandingOfThisAddition: This is an authoring change to an UNAPPLIED candidate at schemaVersion 1 that has never shipped - not a change to a published major - so the may-never-change rules are not engaged by it. Were this schema published, adding a required member would be a major break by this contract's own rules.

recordMembers.name: enforcementDisclosure
recordMembers.shapeUntilTheActorDecisionAndDr105Close: RESERVED BINDING POINT: { reserved: true, ridesOn: ['DR-105'], conditionedOn: 'the ACTOR decision at ID-DEP-12' }
recordMembers.semantics: THE CARRIER for the per-cell enforcement disclosure the DR-105 candidate states as a binding obligation on the host's machine output and audit - the enforcement state carried verbatim in its own vocabulary, never softened, with silence expressly not counting as disclosure. An independent coherence review measured that this obligation has NO carrier anywhere in the pair: that candidate states the obligation and names no surface that discharges it, and v1 named disclosure honesty repeatedly while binding no member to it. Doctor's report is the machine output, so doctor is the natural and probably the only carrier.
recordMembers.theSplitThisMemberDraws: Doctor owns WHERE the string is emitted and that it is emitted affirmatively rather than by silence. DR-105 owns WHAT THE STRING SAYS - its four-member enforcement vocabulary is that candidate's, and this contract's three-value `execution` member cannot express two of its values (route-only enforcement carrying a mandatory paired disclosure, and genuine non-determination). That is a difference of AXIS, not a vocabulary this contract should widen (sharedTermDisambiguation, 'enforced').
recordMembers.ifTheActorDecisionLeavesHostSurfacesOuts: The member is WITHDRAWN, not populated with a doctor-invented string. Supplying a carrier for an obligation that turns out not to reach doctor is a member with nothing to carry, and this contract would rather delete it than fill it.

recordMembers.name: argumentVector
recordMembers.semantics: DISCLOSURE of the exact descriptor-controlled argument vector doctor passed, for CA-1 and CA-2. Bounded and redaction-classified like every other report string. Null with an explicit reason for CA-3 and CA-4, where nothing is executed. This member exists so that what actually ran is visible in the post-report WITHOUT the consent being scoped by it: v1 bound CA-2's consent to 'the exact argument vector', which is the argument-level policy surface the DR-105 candidate reserved to DR-125 under another word. The binding is withdrawn and the disclosure kept (boundsAreNotPermissionParameters). Nothing here decides which arguments a program may receive; that policy is another row's to mint.

mandatoryPostReport.postReportIsNotOptional: A consented action whose record cannot be written is a report-integrity failure, not a silent success: it produces outcome class OC-5 (doctorFault) rather than a report missing a record.

boundsAreNotPermissionParameters.why: An independent coherence review measured three concepts in v1's consent scopes as permission-shaped bounds minted under a different word: a wall-clock deadline, a byte budget, and argument-vector scoping. Two of the three are surfaces DR-105 expressly reserved or ruled out, and the third is a parameter shape its vocabulary has no grammar for. MENTIONING is not CARRYING, and its converse holds too: binding a policy surface under a word that is not its name is minting by semantic duplication. This section states what each bound IS, so that none of them can be read as a permission parameter.
boundsAreNotPermissionParameters.theRule: Every bound doctor carries on a consented action is one of exactly two things: an OBSERVATION OR IO BOUND on doctor's own behavior, or a DISCLOSURE MEMBER in the mandatory post-report. Neither is a permission scope parameter, neither authorizes anything, and neither orders anything against anything else. Where a bound could be read as authorization, it is stated here as not being one.

bounds.bound: the DEADLINE on every consented action
bounds.whatItIs: A bound on how long doctor waits before it stops observing. Exceeding it yields a check with status UNDETERMINED and cause observation-bounded - the same BOUNDED READS rule that governs every other read doctor performs (degradedAndHostileInputs.hostileInputDiscipline). It is recorded in the post-report as part of what the consent carried.
bounds.whatItIsNot: It is NOT an expiry, and doctor's clock decides no authorization and no order. DR-105's R-10 rules that an expiry 'is materialized as a journaled record at the sequence where the host observes it' and is expressly 'NOT evaluated by comparing a wall-clock expiry timestamp against a wall-clock now at commit time; doing so would make the clock the order, which DR-G09 forbids' - and the register's DR-G09 waiver-rule cell reads 'wall-clock/component ordering is forbidden' (both re-measured at the digests recorded in recordedInputs).
bounds.whyItIsOutsideThatProhibition: By construction, not by promise. A deadline that fires ends an OBSERVATION and produces UNDETERMINED, which is not success-bearing; it can therefore make doctor say less, and can never make an unauthorized action authorized, cancel an authorization, or place two records in an order. Nothing in this contract compares a stored expiry timestamp against now to decide whether an act may proceed, because this contract stores no such timestamp: a doctor consent expires with the invocation and is never persisted. DEG-6 tests the property under a skewed clock.
bounds.ifTheActorDecisionMakesADoctorConsentAGr: Then an EXPIRY in DR-105's sense is a journaled record ordered at the sequence where the host observes it, and doctor supplies no such record and holds no sequence numbers. The expiry mechanism would have to come from DR-105's side, and this deadline would remain a separate observation bound sitting beside it. Named at actorMismatch; not decided here.

bounds.bound: the BYTE CAP on bytes doctor accepts, and the BYTE COUNTS reported afterwards
bounds.whatItIs: Two different things that v1 ran together. The CAP is doctor's own bound on how many bytes it will read into its report from a component's output, a customer tool's output, or a network response - a resource bound on doctor, enforced by doctor, whose breach yields UNDETERMINED with cause observation-bounded. The COUNTS are file 04's own post-report obligation, whose words are 'endpoint/bytes where relevant', carried at the `bytes` record member.
bounds.whatItIsNot: The cap is NOT a volume allowance on a grant. DR-105's scope parameters are enumerations of NAMES - path prefixes, variable names, program identifiers, endpoint sets, state classes - and that vocabulary has no grammar for a quantitative volume bound. This contract does not invent one and does not ask DR-105 to honor one; a scope expression a vocabulary has no grammar for is not reserved room, it is an invention.

bounds.bound: the ARGUMENT VECTOR of a consented execution
bounds.whatItIs: Two things, and only the first is doctor's. (1) An IO DISCIPLINE: any consented execution passes a descriptor-controlled argument vector and never a shell string. That is doctor's own rule about its own process boundary, carried from the prototype's measured single-IO-boundary discipline and stated at hostileInputDiscipline. (2) A DISCLOSURE: what was actually passed is recorded in the post-report at the `argumentVector` member, so a reader can see what ran.
bounds.whatItIsNot: It is NOT a consent scope parameter, and this contract mints no argument-level POLICY. the DR-105 candidate's declared-program execution token states in its own scopeParameter (/permissionVocabulary/tokens/3, quoted at that candidate's digest) that 'Argument vectors are NOT scoped by this token; argument-level policy is not designed here and is a RESERVED extension point', and its reserved extension point for argument-vector scoping (/permissionVocabulary/reservedExtensionPoints/3) assigns minting to 'DR-125, or a successor to this contract'. v1 bound CA-2's consent to 'the exact argument vector' under the word scopeBound, which is that reserved surface under another name. The binding is withdrawn; the IO discipline and the disclosure remain, and neither decides which arguments a program may receive.

boundsAreNotPermissionParameters.whatThisDoesNotWeaken: Nothing operational. Doctor still refuses to pass a shell string, still bounds every read, still terminates at its deadline, and still reports the vector, the endpoint and the byte counts afterwards. What changed is that none of these is offered as an authorization parameter to a vocabulary that has no place for it.

sharedTermDisambiguation.why: An independent coherence review measured NINE shared terms that the DR-105 candidate and this contract use with different referents, and found that neither artifact names the other's identifiers anywhere: zero DR-105 token strings in this artifact, zero CA-n identifiers in that one. Two artifacts that never collide on a name and disagree on every meaning are the harder failure, because a joined implementation reads one word and gets whichever sense it happened to load. This section states, on THIS artifact's side only, which sense each term carries here. It does not restate the other artifact's definitions as authority and it does not adopt them; each is cited at that candidate's digest as a candidate.

terms.senseHere: A DISCLOSURE MEMBER of the mandatory post-report, carrying the exact bound the consent carried: which checks, which target identity, which enumerated resources, which platform. It is held for the invocation and never persisted.
terms.senseThere: A typed, per-token DATA PARAMETER on a durable grant - a path-prefix list, variable names, program identifiers, an endpoint set, a state class - journaled, with a narrowing itself a record carrying its own sequence number.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: The member KEEPS the name, because `scope` is file 04's own word in the obligation this contract discharges - 'Every consented action reports scope, endpoint/bytes where relevant, result, and residual limitation' - and renaming the source's word to avoid a collision would be this contract editing its own obligation text. Instead the non-identity is stated: doctor's `scope` is NOT DR-105's grant scope parameter, and a scope-exceeded refusal in that candidate's sense is not decidable against it, because there is no durable scope record for a later act to exceed. A joined implementation must not read one for the other.

terms.senseHere: The value of the post-report's `authorization` member, taken verbatim from file 03's first record: 'requested', then resolved to 'granted' or 'denied'.
terms.senseThere: An authorization record, durably ordered, that 'Confers PERMISSION, not CAPABILITY' and that on a disclosure-only row 'changes nothing about what the component can do'.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: The two are compatible and v2 states the compatibility rather than relying on it. A doctor `authorization: granted` record confers no capability by itself either: what makes a consented action happen is doctor performing it, and the record is the account of what was asked and answered, never a claim that the act was contained. Where the act's confinement is the question, the `execution` member answers it and is constrained by this contract to say 'disclosed-trusted-code' rather than 'enforced' absent measured confinement. Doctor's granted is OPERATIONALLY CONSEQUENTIAL in a way a component's is not - doctor is the actor - and that difference is a fact about who acts, which is the routed actor question, not a disagreement this contract can settle by wording.

terms.senseHere: One of exactly three values of the post-report's `execution` member, file 03's second record: 'enforced', 'disclosed-trusted-code', 'refused'. It is a per-ACTION record about confinement.
terms.senseThere: A per-(platform, token, execution-mode) CELL value from a four-member vocabulary, each value requiring a named mechanism and a stated scope of claim.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: DIFFERENT AXES, not a vocabulary this contract should widen: one is a record about one action doctor took, the other is a standing property of a platform/token/mode cell. This contract's three values are file 03's own and are not doctor's to extend. What v1 lacked was a CARRIER for the other axis, which is supplied at the post-report's `enforcementDisclosure` member as a reserved binding point - see that member. On honesty the two artifacts already agree exactly: recording 'enforced' without measured confinement is the claim file 03's confinement-honesty section forbids, and FC-POSTREPORT fails on it.

terms.senseHere: Two uses, both doctor-side: a claim stated as disclosure rather than guarantee (the redaction two-tier split), and the `disclosed-trusted-code` execution value.
terms.senseThere: A binding OBLIGATION on the host's machine output and audit, derived from the enforcement value, requiring the enforcement state be carried verbatim in its own vocabulary and never softened, with 'Silence is not disclosure'.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: The review's sharpest observation on this axis is that doctor's report is the natural and probably the ONLY carrier for that obligation, and that v1 bound no member to it - naming disclosure honesty repeatedly while carrying nobody's disclosure obligation, which is MENTIONING rather than CARRYING. v2 supplies the CARRIER and not the vocabulary: `enforcementDisclosure` on the consent record is a RESERVED BINDING POINT riding DR-105, in the same idiom as permissionRef. Doctor owns where the string is emitted; DR-105 owns what the string says. If the routed actor decision leaves host surfaces outside the vocabulary, the member is withdrawn rather than populated - it never becomes doctor's to fill.

terms.senseHere: TRUST-STATE revocation only, in every one of this artifact's occurrences: a component, index or core artifact appearing in the recorded last-known revocation state, read as a RECORDED value and riding DR-112 (ID-DEP-6, DEG-4).
terms.senseThere: The grant-generation linearization point, with stated meanings and non-meanings, at which a permission grant ceases to authorize.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: DISJOINT REFERENTS, stated so a reader of the pair does not read one as the other. This contract defines NO revocation of a consent, and its silence is not a gap it is hiding: a doctor consent expires with the invocation and is never persisted, so there is no standing grant for a revocation to reach. Whether a doctor consent is the kind of object that can be revoked mid-operation is the routed actor decision, and the revoke-mid-probe scenario has no determinate answer on the pair's current bytes.

terms.senseHere: ABSENT from v1 by measurement - zero occurrences - and now named. Three of this contract's four consentable action classes initiate effects for which the host holds no inverse: CA-1 and CA-2 because a spawned process may have done anything before it is reaped, and CA-4 because bytes that have left the host cannot be recalled.
terms.senseThere: A fail-closed default over every effect class, with egress irreversible by a class rule no declaration may override, and declared-program execution irreversible.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: The PROPERTY is acknowledged; the MECHANISM is absent and the absence is stated rather than implied. Doctor writes no pre-commit record, holds no commit-intent ordering, and has no pre-commit gate: it initiates the action and writes ONE consent record afterwards. Whether an ordered, durable record must precede initiation is exactly the routed actor decision - the requirement exists only if a doctor consent is a journal grant - so this contract names the property, states that it has no mechanism for it, and does not build one on a question that is not its to answer. What it does do unconditionally is refuse rather than proceed where an irreversible effect would occur outside a named consent (consentDoesNotCascade.theHardCase).

terms.senseHere: A doctor-side observation bound. See boundsAreNotPermissionParameters, which states this at full width.
terms.senseThere: A journaled RECORD materialized at the sequence where the host observes it, where 'The expiry RECORD, not the expiry TIME, is what other records are ordered against.'
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: The two artifacts use disjoint words for what a reader would take to be the same bound - zero occurrences of 'deadline' in that candidate, zero of 'sequence number' here - and v2 bridges them by stating that they are NOT the same bound. Doctor's deadline ends an observation; it expires no authorization and orders nothing.

terms.senseHere: UNDETERMINED is a check status and 'a statement about DOCTOR's reach, not about the environment': an input was unreadable, a dependency absent, an observation bounded out, or a source changed under observation.
terms.senseThere: INDETERMINATE is an OUTCOME of an effect - the host does not know whether an external irreversible effect landed - explicitly not a refusal, never guessed, retried, or resolved by recovery.
terms.thisArtifactsPosition: NEAR-HOMOGRAPHS WITH MATERIALLY DIFFERENT CONTENT, and collapsing them is FORBIDDEN by this contract, not merely discouraged. Reporting 'doctor could not reach a verdict' for a case whose actual content is 'bytes may have left this host and nobody knows' would be the strongest form of the collapse this contract's honesty rule exists to prevent. The two live on different objects - UNDETERMINED on a check, an effect outcome on a consent record - and v2 keeps them structurally apart by giving the effect outcome its own member rather than borrowing the status set. See mandatoryPostReport.recordMembers `effectOutcome`.

governingRule.verbatim: The V1 rule applies to **resolved configuration secret values and credentials**. They are referenced by handles; the handle participates where the exact contract requires it, while the value is excluded from PlanId, evidence digest, diagnostics, and support bundles.
governingRule.whyItReachesDoctor: Doctor output IS diagnostics. The exclusion is therefore already binding on doctor's report by the preserved V1 rule; this section does not create the obligation, it states the bound and the corpus of cases.
governingRule.expressLimitVerbatim: This rule does not classify arbitrary analyzed source text as a configuration secret and does not promise that code authorized to read source cannot observe credentials embedded in that source.

twoTierStructure.why: The corpus's honesty discipline requires that a redaction claim which cannot be enforced be stated as DISCLOSURE, not GUARANTEE. Doctor's report contains two materially different kinds of string, and one claim cannot honestly cover both. So the contract states two tiers with different standings, and every report member is classified into exactly one.

tier1.name: GUARANTEE tier - host-constructed members over classified sources
tier1.what: Report members that doctor CONSTRUCTS from sources whose classification the host already knows: resolved configuration values carrying a secret classification, credential handles, declared credential environment variable names, manifest-declared fields, custody digests, platform facts, and the environment block.
tier1.guarantee: For these members the guarantee is exact and structural: a value classified secret NEVER enters the report in any form - not raw, not truncated, not previewed, not hashed into a member that a reader could use as an oracle. What enters is the HANDLE and a presence boolean. The guarantee is enforceable because it is a property of the construction path: doctor never has the value in a report-bound member to begin with.
tier1.bound: The guarantee covers exactly the members doctor constructs from classified sources. It is a guarantee about doctor's construction, not about the universe of secrets.

tier2.name: DISCLOSURE tier - free text from outside doctor's construction
tier2.what: Any string doctor did not construct: a component's bounded fault detail, a consented tool's captured output, an error message, a path an operator chose, a manifest's free-text field.
tier2.disclosure: These strings are pattern-scrubbed against known credential shapes, control-character stripped, ANSI-neutralized, and length-bounded before they enter the report. This is BEST EFFORT AND IS NOT A GUARANTEE. Pattern scrubbing catches known shapes; it does not catch arbitrary high-entropy strings, novel credential formats, secrets a tool prints in a format nobody anticipated, or a secret an operator embedded in a filename.
tier2.measuredBasis: The prototype's own redaction machinery states this bound in its source, measured at packages/external-tool-adapter/src/redact.ts (53b46f8d...): 'Conservative by design - it targets known credential shapes, not arbitrary high-entropy strings.' The three implemented families are URL userinfo, Bearer/Basic auth-scheme tokens, and inline key=value credential assignments. The V2 contract carries the honest bound forward as a STRUCTURAL two-tier claim rather than a source comment.
tier2.whyNotUpgradeIt: Alternative considered and rejected: declare a single redaction guarantee covering all report strings, backed by an entropy heuristic. Rejected because an entropy heuristic produces both false negatives (a low-entropy passphrase passes) and false positives (a legitimate digest is destroyed), and because a guarantee that fails on unanticipated input is exactly the unenforceable claim this corpus requires to be stated as disclosure. The bound is the claim.

defaultRedactedClasses.class: resolved configuration secret values and credentials
defaultRedactedClasses.treatment: Never present. Handle plus presence boolean only. Tier 1.
Never present. Presence boolean only, and only for variables a manifest DECLARES (see DIFF-7). Tier 1.

Project-relative where inside the project root; a non-identifying marker otherwise. The prototype's projectRelativePath is the measured baseline. Tier 1 for paths doctor constructs; tier 2 for paths that arrive inside free text.
Never present: hostname, username, home directory, machine identifier, network address. Tier 1 (environmentBlock.expresslyExcluded).
Password half masked. Tier 2 pattern family.
Never present. Name plus scrubbed message only, with an explicit marker that the object was redacted - the prototype's deny-by-default posture, carried.

Stripped before any string enters the report, ANSI first then C0 controls (the prototype's measured ordering, which exists because ESC is itself a control code). Not a confidentiality measure - a report-integrity and terminal-safety measure against hostile input.
Length-bounded with an explicit truncation marker. An unbounded string from a hostile component is a denial-of-service and a leak surface at once.

secretPreviewsAreForbidden.rule: The doctor report never carries a secret PREVIEW - not a first-N-characters mask, not a last-N-characters mask, and not a truncated hash presented as an identity.
secretPreviewsAreForbidden.measuredContrast: The prototype's redactSecret returns the first 4 characters plus an ellipsis, and secretHash returns 12 hex characters of the value's sha256. Both are defensible in their prototype context (telling two findings apart in a secret-scanner's output) and both are wrong for a doctor report, where no check needs to distinguish two secrets. See DIFF-8.

whatTheGuaranteeExplicitlyDoesNotCover.form: Stated in the honest-exclusion form file 04's purge section uses, where the exclusions are part of the contract rather than a caveat: purge 'names OpenSIP-controlled evidence, state, caches, and closures and honestly excludes backups, filesystem snapshots, dumps, swap, external/remote stores, and user copies.'
exclusions: ANALYZED SOURCE TEXT. File 03 is express: the secret rule 'does not classify arbitrary analyzed source text as a configuration secret'. A credential committed into a repository is not a configuration secret and doctor does not treat it as one. Doctor does not read analyzed source at all in either mode, so the exclusion is mostly moot for doctor - but it is stated because a reader who assumes doctor scrubs source-derived material would be wrong.
ARBITRARY HIGH-ENTROPY STRINGS. Tier 2 catches known shapes only. A novel credential format passes through.

SECRETS IN NAMES THE OPERATOR CHOSE. A filename, directory name, project name, or component alias containing a credential is reported as the name it is. Doctor cannot distinguish a secret in a path segment from a path segment.
OUTPUT OF A CONSENTED CUSTOMER TOOL, beyond tier-2 scrubbing and byte bounds. A CA-2 tool's output is unbounded by OpenSIP by construction.

ANYTHING OUTSIDE THE REPORT BYTES. Terminal scrollback, CI job logs, shell history of the invocation, a support bundle an operator assembles by hand, and any copy an operator makes are outside doctor's reach entirely. Doctor's guarantee is over the bytes it emits.

THE FACT OF EXISTENCE. Redaction hides values, not structure. A doctor report discloses that a credential is configured, which component declares it, and which check needed it. That disclosure is intentional - it is what makes the report useful - and it is named here so nobody mistakes value redaction for existence redaction.

SIDE CHANNELS OF A CONSENTED ACTION. A CA-4 egress discloses to the far side; a CA-3 keychain probe may prompt the operator's OS. Redaction of the report does not un-disclose what the action itself disclosed.

redaction.redactionAppliesToEveryProjection: The guarantee and disclosure both attach to the REPORT, not to a renderer. Human output, machine output, and any future projection are projections of the same redacted report; a renderer never sees an unredacted value and therefore cannot leak one. File 02 already assigns projection to the host ('host-owned human, JSON, and applicable SARIF projection') and forbids components rendering product UI directly, so this is the corpus's existing shape rather than a new rule.

The code VALUES are DR-007-owned and DR-007's row is HARD-BLOCKED, with the blueprint-impact cell reading 'V2 cannot define replay/purge/degradation typed result or exit'.
