theResolution.howTheCorpusResolvesThis: Bind the STRUCTURE, name the owner of the values, carry the symmetry clause, assign no number. This artifact defines which outcome classes exist, what distinguishes each from its neighbours, and which are success-bearing. It assigns no exit code, mints no D9 code, and names no fault cause.
whatIsBoundHere: the outcome classes and their distinguishing properties
the rule that determines the report's outcome class from its checks
the rule that a report whose own integrity failed cannot present as any environment verdict
whatIsNotBoundHere: the optional-presence, success/policy/interrupted branch structure DR-007's row names

outcomeClasses.name: allChecksSatisfied
outcomeClasses.distinguishedBy: Every check in the report has a success-bearing status (PASS or NOT-APPLICABLE), and no report-level residual limitation is present that bears on a check's verdict.
outcomeClasses.note: The ONLY success-bearing outcome class. It is deliberately hard to reach: a single UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED check disqualifies it.

outcomeClasses.name: environmentDefectFound
outcomeClasses.distinguishedBy: At least one check has status FAIL, and the report is COMPLETE - doctor reached a verdict on everything it attempted. The statement is about the ENVIRONMENT: doctor worked, and found something wrong.
outcomeClasses.note: This is the class CI gates on. Its distinguishing property against OC-3 is report completeness, not severity.

outcomeClasses.name: reportIncomplete
outcomeClasses.distinguishedBy: At least one check has status UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED, and no check has status FAIL. The statement is about DOCTOR's REACH: doctor could not answer everything it was asked, and is saying so rather than presenting a partial report as a clean bill.
outcomeClasses.note: The single most important class in this structure. Collapsing OC-3 into OC-1 is the failure mode where an environment nobody could inspect reports healthy; collapsing it into OC-2 is the failure mode where 'we could not look' is indistinguishable from 'we looked and it is broken', which sends an operator to fix a defect that may not exist. Where a report contains BOTH a FAIL and an UNDETERMINED, the outcome is OC-2 with the incompleteness carried in report-level residual limitations - because a known defect is the more actionable statement, and the incompleteness is not lost, only subordinated.

outcomeClasses.name: invocationRefused
outcomeClasses.distinguishedBy: Doctor refused to run the invocation as asked and produced no check results: a named consent was required by the invocation but denied by policy, the invocation is malformed, the requested mode is unavailable, or a requested schemaVersion is unsupported. The statement is about the INVOCATION, and it is made BEFORE any check runs.
outcomeClasses.note: Distinct from OC-2 and OC-3 because there is no environment verdict at all - not even a partial one. A refusal that presented as OC-3 would imply doctor tried.

outcomeClasses.name: doctorFault
outcomeClasses.distinguishedBy: Doctor itself failed: it could not construct its report, could not write a required consent record, or could not emit the report to its output sink. The statement is about DOCTOR, not the environment and not the invocation.
outcomeClasses.note: Required as its own class because DR-123's acceptance cell names 'output-failure' evidence among what every first-slice core command must show, and because a doctor whose output sink failed must not exit as though the environment were fine. A report that cannot be emitted is the one case where the machine schema cannot carry the outcome, so the outcome must survive in the exit alone - which is precisely why the class must exist structurally even though its value is DR-007's.

successPartition.rule: Exactly one outcome class is success-bearing. Four distinct non-success classes exist because they answer four different operator questions - is my environment broken, did doctor fail to look, did doctor decline to run, did doctor itself break - and an operator who cannot tell them apart cannot act.

outcomeStructure.derivationRule: The report's outcome class is DERIVED from the check statuses by the following total, deterministic rule, evaluated in order: if the report could not be constructed or emitted, OC-5; else if no check ran because the invocation was refused, OC-4; else if any check is FAIL, OC-2; else if any check is UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED, OC-3; else OC-1. The rule is stated so two conforming implementations agree on the class from the same check set, and so a reader can verify the class against the checks rather than trusting it.

dr007Ride.ownership: DR-007's successor owns every VALUE: the exit code for each outcome class, the D9 code if any, and the fault cause for any doctor-observed failure. This artifact provides the classes for that successor to map, and nothing more.
dr007Ride.measuredStanding: DR-007 row measured at the file 08 digest: status HARD-BLOCKED; required acceptance evidence 'D9 successor for observation→faultCause, optional presence, success/policy/interrupted branch, plus reviewed retention degradation/refusal integration without invented codes'; blueprint impact 'V2 cannot define replay/purge/degradation typed result or exit'.
dr007Ride.symmetryClause: If DR-007's successor closes by scoped disposition rather than binding codes, doctor's D9/exit mapping ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits, by that disposition's terms. The outcome-class STRUCTURE survives such a disposition because it contains no value; what does not survive is any expectation that doctor has an exit contract before DR-007 closes. None of it survives on prose.
dr007Ride.explicitNonAssignment: No number appears in this section. The prototype's EXIT_CODES values are recorded in recordedInputs for the DIFF record only (DIFF-3) and are not proposed, carried, or implied here - including the prototype's use of CONFIGURATION_ERROR for a not-ready doctor, which this contract expressly does not adopt.

degradedAndHostileInputs.whyThisIsTheCore: Doctor is the surface users reach WHEN THINGS ARE BROKEN. Its behavior on broken input is therefore the contract's core, not an edge case: a doctor that works only on a healthy install is a status command. Three cross-cutting laws hold across every case below, and each case then states the specific trap that case sets. SEVEN cases are enumerated (DEG-1..DEG-7). The enumeration is NOT claimed exhaustive over the broken-state space, and the cases outside it that this contract knows of are named at degradedAndHostileInputs.casesWithNoSeparateEntry rather than left for a reader to discover as silence.

crossCuttingLaws.law: DOCTOR ALWAYS PRODUCES A REPORT. No degraded or hostile input causes doctor to crash, hang, or emit nothing. Where a check cannot be answered, the check is present with status UNDETERMINED and a residual limitation naming what blocked it. The only case in which no report is emitted is OC-5, where the sink itself failed - and even then the outcome survives in the exit.

DOCTOR NEVER REPAIRS. Nothing in this section is a licence to fix, clear, refresh, rebuild, quarantine, roll back, or complete anything. Repair is DR-110's surface; migration is the lifecycle surface's prepare/commit/abort; the read-only and no-mutation defaults have no consented departure (consentModel.defaultPosture.twoOfFourAreAbsolute). Doctor's whole value on a broken install is that it changes nothing while the operator decides.

DOCTOR NEVER FALLS BACK TO A DIFFERENT QUESTION. Where the intended input is unavailable, doctor reports that it is unavailable; it does not silently answer an easier question with the same check id. This is the specific discipline file 02 already requires of analysis ('no silent fallback to a weaker syntactic, semantic, or graph answer') applied to diagnosis, and it is what makes the report's check ids trustworthy across invocations.

cases.input: Corrupt install - the installed generation's bytes do not match its recorded inventory digests, or the inventory itself is unreadable.
cases.behavior: INSTALL-INTEGRITY checks report FAIL for each entry whose measured digest differs from its recorded digest, with the entry identity and both digest facts as evidence; entries doctor cannot read at all report UNDETERMINED with cause input-unreadable. Every check class that DEPENDS on the corrupt region reports UNDETERMINED rather than PASS, and the dependency is named in the residual limitation - a component-inventory check that read a corrupt index cannot honestly pass.
cases.theTrap: Doctor's own executable may be part of the corrupt closure. Doctor does not claim to have verified itself: an integrity check whose verifier is inside the region being verified reports its own scope as a residual limitation rather than asserting a self-clean result. Where the corruption prevents doctor from reading its own inventory, the honest outcome is OC-3, not OC-2.
cases.outcomeClass: OC-2 where a defect is measured; OC-3 where doctor could not measure.

cases.input: Unreadable lock - the project lock is absent, truncated, malformed, contains a duplicate key, or cannot be parsed.
cases.behavior: LOCK-STATE checks report UNDETERMINED with cause input-unreadable and a residual limitation naming the exact failure (absent / unparseable / duplicate key, with the duplicated key NAMED). Every project-scoped check whose evidence would come from the lock's selections also reports UNDETERMINED. Doctor STAYS IN PROJECT MODE (modes.modeSelection.whyNoSilentDowngrade).
cases.theTrap: The tempting behavior is to resolve without the lock and report on what would happen - which answers a question the operator did not ask, about a configuration nobody runs, under the same check ids. DL-3 forbids it. Equally forbidden: rewriting, regenerating, or 'healing' the lock (DL-2), and treating an absent lock as equivalent to a lock selecting nothing.
cases.duplicateKeyRule: A duplicate key in any document doctor parses is a parse REFUSAL for that document, not a last-key-wins read, and the refusal NAMES the duplicated key. This follows the corpus's existing duplicate-key discipline as recorded in the component-manifest candidate (cited at digest, candidate standing) rather than inventing a parsing posture: last-key-wins lets a document say one thing to a reader and another to every instrument while its bytes stay unchanged, which for a diagnostic surface means the report could describe a configuration the host would never resolve.

cases.input: Missing component - the lock or index references a component whose bytes are not installed.
cases.behavior: COMPONENT-INVENTORY reports FAIL with the referenced component identity, the referencing record, and the absence as evidence. COMPONENT-LIVENESS for that component reports NOT-APPLICABLE (there is nothing to start) rather than CONSENT-REQUIRED - the distinction matters because CONSENT-REQUIRED implies an answer is obtainable by naming consent, and here it is not. Any remediation record names an operator action; it never triggers one.
cases.theTrap: A missing payload must not trigger a download, a refresh, or a lock mutation. File 04's offline section states this as a law for the system; doctor is the surface most likely to be written as a helpful exception to it, and it is not one. Doctor reports absence and stops.

cases.input: Revoked signature - a component, index, or core artifact appears in the recorded last-known revocation state, or its signature does not verify against current recorded roots.
cases.behavior: TRUST-STATE reports FAIL with the revocation or verification fact as evidence, taken from RECORDED state. The report carries the AGE of the last-known revocation state and the recorded metadata expiry in environment.offlinePosture, and a residual limitation stating that revocation state is as-of that recorded moment and may be stale.
cases.theTrap: The tempting behavior is to refresh revocation state to answer accurately - which is egress. It requires named CA-4 consent, and absent that consent doctor reports the recorded state WITH its staleness rather than a fresher state it did not obtain. Equally: doctor does not advance, clear, or roll back any trust state, which file 04 requires to be 'separate monotonic state' that never rolls back with executable pointers.
cases.escalationHonesty: A revoked-but-still-installed component is reported as a defect; whether it may CONTINUE to run is the reviewed offline-running policy's decision (file 04) and DR-112's state machine, not doctor's. Doctor reports the fact and names the owning surface; it issues no verdict on continued operation.

cases.input: Partially migrated state - a migration is prepared but not committed, aborted mid-flight, or left state at an ambiguous point after a crash.
cases.behavior: STATE-CLASS-HEALTH reports the migration's recorded position in the prepare/commit/abort ladder as evidence, with status FAIL where the state is measurably inconsistent and UNDETERMINED where doctor cannot determine which side of a transition the state is on. Where file 04's rule has already applied - 'After a crash, ambiguous bytes or state fail closed and quarantine' - doctor reports the quarantine as a fact, since quarantine is the lifecycle surface's correct outcome and not itself a doctor defect.
cases.theTrap: Doctor must not resume, complete, abort, or roll back the migration, and must not clear a quarantine. It also must not report a prepared-not-committed migration as corruption: prepare is a legitimate state in the ladder, and the check distinguishes 'mid-ladder' from 'inconsistent'. The no-return boundary each migration declares is reported where recorded, never inferred.
cases.outcomeClass: OC-2 or OC-3 depending on determinability.

cases.input: Untrustworthy clock - the host time source is skewed, has jumped, or is otherwise not a reliable measure of elapsed time. Includes a clock moved backwards between doctor's own reads.
cases.behavior: Doctor reports RECORDED TIMESTAMPS as the primary evidence and any derived AGE as a secondary, explicitly derived value. environment.offlinePosture carries the recorded revocation and metadata-expiry timestamps alongside any age computed from them, so a reader can recompute rather than trust doctor's arithmetic. Where a TRUST-STATE check's verdict would rest on elapsed time and doctor cannot establish that the time source is trustworthy, the check reports UNDETERMINED with cause observation-bounded and a residual limitation naming the clock as the input doctor could not establish. A check whose verdict rests only on recorded values that do not depend on elapsed time (a signature that does not verify, an artifact present in the recorded revocation state) is unaffected and still reports FAIL.
cases.theTrap: Reporting a confidently wrong staleness. DEG-4's entire honesty rests on reporting the AGE of the last-known revocation state, and an age is a clock difference; under skew doctor would report a precise number that is wrong, which is worse than reporting that it cannot tell. File 04's rule at lines 221-222 - 'Expired or future metadata cannot be partially understood' - is itself clock-dependent, so doctor must not decide expiry from its own clock and then present the decision as a measured fact. The second trap is the opposite one: treating skew as a reason to refresh, which is egress and needs CA-4.
cases.whyThisCannotBecomeAnAuthorizationDefect: Doctor's deadlines are OBSERVATION bounds, never authorization or ordering parameters (consentModel.boundsAreNotPermissionParameters). A skewed clock can therefore end an observation early or late - producing UNDETERMINED, which is not success-bearing - but it can never make an unauthorized action authorized, expire a consent, or order two records against each other. That is the register's DR-G09 waiver-rule cell ('wall-clock/component ordering is forbidden', re-measured at the register digest recorded in recordedInputs) honored structurally rather than by promise.
cases.whatDoctorDoesNotOwn: Doctor mints no time authority and names none. Whether the corpus binds a trustworthy time source is DR-112's, whose surface already carries the corpus's answer to an untrustworthy clock: file 04 line 78 names 'trust roots, revocation observations, expiry floors, and anti-rollback counters' as separate monotonic state. Doctor reports recorded counters and floors as facts and derives nothing from its own clock that it presents as a verdict (ID-DEP-6).
cases.outcomeClass: OC-3 where a verdict rested on an age doctor could not establish; OC-2 where a defect is measured from recorded values independent of elapsed time.

cases.input: Concurrent mutation - another process (an update, a garbage collection, a repair, or a second doctor) is mutating the install inventory, component index custody records, the project lock, or state while doctor is reading them.
cases.behavior: Doctor detects rather than prevents. Each state source doctor reads has its IDENTITY measured when first read and re-measured at the end of the invocation - the recorded digest, the generation identity, or the custody record's own version, whichever that source already carries; doctor mints none of them (ID-DEP-10). Any source whose identity differs between the two measurements makes EVERY check that consumed it report UNDETERMINED with cause source-changed-under-observation and a residual limitation naming the source and both observed identities. Checks that consumed only stable sources are unaffected and keep their verdicts.
cases.theTrap: Two traps, in opposite directions. FIRST: presenting a torn composite as a fact. Doctor reads lock, install inventory, index custody and state at different instants; without detection it can report a combination that never existed at any instant, which is a false report produced by a surface whose whole value is a truthful snapshot, and which DL-3 (never answer a different question under the same check id) already forbids in spirit. SECOND, and the reason doctor does not simply take a lock: file 04 lines 71-74 record that 'active processes hold generation leases/refcounts and open references needed for safe completion/recovery' and that 'remove and GC cannot delete bytes/state referenced by locks, active processes, retained evidence, rollback slots, or prepared migrations'. A doctor that acquired a lease or refcount to buy itself consistency would become a participant in the lifecycle's concurrency control and could block a GC or an update from completing - a diagnostic changing the thing it diagnoses, which DP-1/DP-4 forbid without consented departure and which DL-2's no-repair rule exists to prevent. Consistency is therefore DETECTED and DISCLOSED, never ACQUIRED.
cases.theHonestBound: Re-read detection is not atomicity and this contract does not claim it is. It catches a source that changed and was not changed back; it does NOT catch a source mutated and restored to an identical identity within the invocation, and it does not order doctor's reads against another process's writes. Under this contract doctor's report can therefore say 'these sources were stable across my invocation' or 'this one moved and I have withdrawn the verdicts that rested on it' - and it can never say the composite was atomic. The bound is the claim.

hostileInputDiscipline.premise: Doctor reads attacker-influenceable bytes: a manifest, a lock, a project configuration file, and - under consent - a component's fault string or a customer tool's output. Every one is untrusted input to a program the operator runs when already worried.
rules: BOUNDED READS. Every read has a size bound and a deadline; exceeding either yields UNDETERMINED with cause observation-bounded, never a truncated value presented as complete.

NO EXECUTION FROM DATA. Nothing doctor reads can cause execution. No path in a manifest, lock, or configuration file is executed, loaded, or resolved as code. Component execution happens only under CA-1 consent against an admitted generation identity.

NO AMBIENT RESOLUTION. Doctor resolves no binary, loader, library, or tool through PATH or any ambient system lookup. File 04's exact-byte-delivery section states the prohibition as a bullet, quoted here with its leading negative intact (lines 152-153): 'no `PATH`, loader, shell, live-project, system-runtime, or install-time substitution; and'. DR-119/D-008 independently forbids ambient lookup for language tooling. The only PATH-shaped case is the declared customer-owned external system, which is identified from its manifest declaration and executed only under CA-2 consent. See DIFF-13.
PARSE REFUSAL OVER BEST EFFORT. Malformed input is refused for that document, with the refusal named as evidence. Doctor does not partially parse a document to extract 'the readable parts'.

TERMINAL AND SINK SAFETY. ANSI sequences are neutralized and control characters stripped before any string enters the report, ANSI first (ESC is itself a control code - the prototype's measured ordering). A hostile component that emits terminal control sequences cannot rewrite an operator's screen through doctor's human projection, and cannot inject structure into doctor's machine projection.

DESCRIPTOR-CONTROLLED ARGUMENTS. Any consented execution passes a descriptor-controlled argument vector, never a shell string - the prototype's measured single-IO-boundary discipline, carried forward as a contract rule rather than a module convention.

REPORT INTEGRITY OVER CONTENT. If hostile input would make the report unemittable or structurally invalid, the outcome is OC-5. A structurally invalid doctor report is worse than no report, because a machine reader will act on it.

casesWithNoSeparateEntry.why: An independent review enumerated a nine-case broken-state space and measured that v1 covered five of it with no disclosure of the omission. Two of the four omissions were material enough to become DEG-6 (clock skew) and DEG-7 (concurrent mutation). The remaining two are closed HERE rather than given their own case, and are named so the omission is disclosed rather than silent.

cases.case: permission denied on doctor's own state (EACCES on a state-class path doctor is entitled to read)
cases.behavior: ABSORBED, and now stated rather than merely absorbable. STATE-CLASS-HEALTH reports UNDETERMINED with cause input-unreadable and a residual limitation naming the state class and the fact that the failure was an access refusal rather than an absence - the two are different operator actions and DL-3 forbids reporting one as the other. DL-1 guarantees the report is still produced. Doctor does not retry with elevated privilege, and does not treat its own inability to read as evidence that the bytes are absent.

cases.pathA: Doctor's OWN Operational-metadata audit write failing for want of space. CLOSED HERE: a consented or default invocation whose audit record cannot be written is a report-integrity failure and produces OC-5 (doctorFault), by the same rule that already governs a consent record that cannot be written (consentModel.mandatoryPostReport.postReportIsNotOptional). FC-RO's accounting is extended for this case so a failed audit write is a PINNED fixture case rather than an undefined region of the read-only property.
cases.pathB: A full disk as a DIAGNOSED CONDITION of the environment. NOT COVERED, and named as absent: no check class in this contract measures free space, and this artifact declines to invent one, because which capacity facts a diagnostic must report is product scope and the check catalog is expressly routed to D-002 blueprint work (stableMachineSchema.scopeOfThisSection). Owning surfaces if it is wanted: the slice-1 check catalog under D-002, with the retained-evidence half at DR-G12. A fixture author must not assume doctor diagnoses capacity.

recordShape.principle: A remediation record is a member of a doctor CHECK, not a standalone object and not an instruction. It names an observation and an operator action. It never carries an executable fix, a command doctor would run, or an exit code.

members.name: remediationClass
members.type: one of the closed set below
members.semantics: The structural category of what the operator must do. Surface-local to the doctor report schema.

members.name: subjectRef
members.semantics: The identity the remediation is about, by REFERENCE to custody records that already exist: the component's stableId and the index entry. No identity is minted here.

members.name: observation
members.semantics: What doctor observed that makes this remediation applicable - e.g. that the resolved configuration or lock references the deprecated name, or that the alias window's recorded end has passed.

members.name: operatorAction
members.semantics: What the operator does. Bounded and redaction-classified like every report string.

members.name: appliedBy
members.semantics: Fixed by construction. There is no other admissible value, and the member exists so the record cannot be misread as something doctor will do. A record whose action doctor could apply would violate DP-1/DP-4, which have no consented departure.

members.name: windowState
members.semantics: For a deprecation remediation: the recorded deprecatedAtRelease, deprecatedAtDate, and windowEndsNoEarlierThan as CARRIED from the manifest candidate's own deprecation members, plus which side of the window the invocation falls on. Doctor reports the window; D-012 clause 5 decides it. Null for remediation records that are not deprecation-driven.

members.name: residualLimitation
members.semantics: What doctor could not establish about the remediation - for example that it could not determine whether every reference to the old name has been updated, because some references live outside OpenSIP's reach.

remediationClasses.name: RENAME-INVOCATION
remediationClasses.meaning: An invocation or script uses the deprecated root command name; the new name resolves the same component. Applicable while the alias window is open.

remediationClasses.name: UPDATE-PIN
remediationClasses.meaning: A resolved configuration value or lock selection references the deprecated name; the reference should be updated to the new name.

remediationClasses.name: WINDOW-OPEN-NO-ACTION-REQUIRED
remediationClasses.meaning: The deprecation is recorded and the window is open; nothing is broken yet. Carried so that a deprecation is VISIBLE before it bites, which is the whole point of the dual clock.

remediationClasses.name: WINDOW-CLOSED-ACTION-REQUIRED
remediationClasses.meaning: The recorded window has ended; the alias no longer resolves and the reference is now a defect.

remediationClasses.name: PREREQUISITE-ABSENT
remediationClasses.meaning: A declared prerequisite - including the DR-119/D-008 customer-owned external-system exception, which file 02 requires to appear 'in manifest and doctor output' - is absent or unsatisfied. This class exists so the DR-119 doctor-output obligation has a carrier in this schema.

expresslyAbsentMembers: any exit code or D9 code (ID-DEP-1)
any command string doctor would execute
an 'automatable' or 'autofix' flag - the member would exist only to be acted on, and acting on it is forbidden
the alias-window POLICY itself, which is D-012's and is referenced, not restated

controlProtocolAlignment.principle: When doctor probes a component it uses the common control plane's existing supervision and refusal vocabulary. It invents no parallel mechanism, no second refusal family, and no doctor-specific message.
controlProtocolAlignment.citationStanding: The vocabulary below is measured from docs/coop/artifacts/control-protocol-contract.v2.json (c50a79fe...), which is status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING. It is cited as a candidate. If DR-102 closes with a different vocabulary, doctor's probe shape follows THAT vocabulary - the alignment obligation survives, the specific message names do not (identityDependencies ID-DEP-4).

functionsDoctorUses.doctorUse: Open supervision, confirm identity binding, observe liveness, close cleanly. This is the whole of a CA-1 liveness probe's session frame.

The evidence a COMPONENT-LIVENESS check actually collects: declared load, bounded resource report, and any internal fault the component reports. A `fault` message's MEANING - fate, D9, exit - is decided under the owning contracts and DR-007's successor, never by the message and never by doctor.

functionsDoctorNeverUses.function: F-3 negotiate an opaque named role subprotocol and version
functionsDoctorNeverUses.why: Sending `select` would open the provider data plane, which is ADM-4. Never sending it is mechanism leg NA-2 of the non-admission argument: without `selectAck`, data-plane bytes are RF-7/CH-DATA-EARLY.

functionsDoctorNeverUses.function: F-5 broker separately authorized host effects
functionsDoctorNeverUses.why: Doctor brokers no effect. A component that sends `effectRequest` during a doctor probe has no valid separate authorization and is refused under RF-6 - doctor does not become an effect broker because it happened to open a channel.

Not a wire function at all in the cited candidate; discovery is host-side reading of admitted metadata, which is exactly what doctor's COMPONENT-INVENTORY class does in the DEFAULT posture with no channel open and no consent.

refusalAlignment.rule: Every refusal doctor encounters or issues on the control channel is one of the cited candidate's RF-1..RF-8 families, recorded as EVIDENCE on the check that provoked it. Doctor mints no refusal family.
refusalAlignment.vocabularyStanding: That candidate's own discipline cell states its families 'are not D9 codes, not exit codes, not fates, and never map to any of those by this artifact'. Doctor honours that: a refusal family appears in a check's evidence and contributes to the check's STATUS, never to an exit value.
refusalAlignment.mappingIntoCheckStatus: An RF-* refusal during a consented probe makes the provoking check FAIL where the refusal is a statement about the component (RF-3 identity-binding-mismatch, RF-4 undeclared-capability, RF-8 handshake-replay-or-downgrade), and UNDETERMINED where the refusal prevented doctor from observing what it came to observe (RF-1 control-version-unsupported, RF-2 frame-violation, RF-7 protocol-state-violation). The consent record's execution value and the check's status are separate records and are both written.

controlProtocolAlignment.supervisionHonesty: Doctor's probe spawns a process. File 03: 'A child process is fault containment, not a sandbox.' The probe's process tree is cancelled and reaped by the host on completion or deadline - the containment behavior DR-G21 covers - and the consent record's execution value is 'disclosed-trusted-code' rather than 'enforced' absent measured confinement.

SCOPE OF THIS PROPERTY, stated in v2: it binds DOCTOR'S OWN WRITES. It is NOT a claim that no other surface wrote during the invocation, and it is expressly NOT decidable today against a tree containing a DR-105 permission grant journal - see theGrantJournalCollision.
failsIf: any byte outside the Operational metadata class changed
the lock changed by any byte
a cache was rebuilt
a quarantine was cleared
a trust or revocation state advanced
a migration moved position in the prepare/commit/abort ladder

The pass property is that NO byte outside the Operational metadata class changed, that the outcome is OC-5, and that the report - if it was emitted at all - does not present an environment verdict. This case exists because FC-RO's accounting rule requires every in-root change to be accounted for by an audit record, and a failed audit write is the one case where that record does not exist.

theGrantJournalCollision.finding: An independent coherence review measured a mechanical collision between this fixture and the DR-105 candidate's acceptance-evidence surface, and noted it is the one finding in that file testable the day both fixture surfaces exist.
theGrantJournalCollision.theCollision: That candidate journals ACCEPTANCE for every request INCLUDING READS - 'a read of a denied path is the refusal this token exists to record' - into a durable, append-only grant journal per (project, grant generation). This fixture fails if ANY byte outside the Operational metadata class changed. If the grant journal lands anywhere but that class, the two fixtures can both be run against the same tree and will contradict: one asserts the journal write is required, the other asserts it is a failure.
theGrantJournalCollision.whyNeitherArtifactCanSettleIt: The journal's state class is UNASSIGNED on both sides. That candidate expressly declines to assign it, recording that the assignment is DR-124's. This contract rides DR-124 for the very definition of the Operational metadata class root this property is stated against (ID-DEP-7). The deciding row is OPEN on both sides.
theGrantJournalCollision.andItIsConditionedOnTheActorDecisionToo: The collision fires only if doctor's consented actions - or doctor's default reads - are DR-105 requests that journal at all, which is the routed actor decision (actorMismatch, ID-DEP-12). Under a disposition that leaves host surfaces outside the vocabulary, no doctor invocation writes a grant journal and this fixture is unaffected.
theGrantJournalCollision.whatThisContractDoesAboutItNow: It NAMES the region rather than weakening the property into vacuity. FC-RO remains a hard byte-immutability property over doctor's own writes and is runnable today. A harness author is instructed here that FC-RO is NOT YET RUNNABLE against a tree in which a DR-105 grant journal is written, and must not be made to pass by widening its exception list to admit journal bytes: widening the exception before DR-124 places the journal would be this contract deciding a state-class assignment it does not own, and would silently retire the strongest property it has.
theGrantJournalCollision.routedTo: DR-124 for the journal's state class, jointly with the ACTOR decision at ID-DEP-12. Both must land before either row's harness is built; the review's own advisory is that the pair's acceptance-evidence surfaces be reconciled before either harness exists.

Under named CA-1 consent: the sentinel is written exactly once, the trace shows exactly one supervised process, and a consent record with actionClass CA-1 is present.

a liveness check reports PASS in the default posture
a liveness check is OMITTED from the report rather than carrying a status
the trace shows a `select` message or any provider data-plane byte (this is also the ADM-4 negative test)

a name is resolved
doctor reports a network-denied environment as an environment defect
the report claims a revocation state fresher than the recorded one
a missing payload triggers a download, refresh, or lock mutation

classes.exactByteIntent: A golden corpus of doctor report bytes: one per mode, one per outcome class OC-1..OC-5, one per check status token, and one per degraded case. Each golden is pinned by sha256. Alongside them, a reader fixture pinned at schemaVersion major 1.
classes.passProperty: The pinned major-1 reader consumes every golden. Adding a new check id, a new check class, a new optional member, a new evidence kind, or a new residual-limitation cause to a golden leaves the reader's verdict on that report UNCHANGED (the additive property). Removing a required member, retyping a member, adding a sixth status token, or moving a token across the success partition causes the reader to REFUSE, not to reinterpret.
failsIf: a reader infers PASS from an absent check or member
a non-executed check is absent rather than statused
an aggregate boolean appears in the envelope
a report from an unsupported future major is partially parsed instead of refused
two conforming producers disagree on the outcome class derived from an identical check set

classes.exactByteIntent: One pinned check-status set per outcome class, paired with the report bytes the derivation rule produces from it - including the two boundary cases: a set containing BOTH a FAIL and an UNDETERMINED (must derive OC-2 with the incompleteness carried at report level), and a set containing only NOT-APPLICABLE and PASS (must derive OC-1).
classes.passProperty: The derivation rule is total and deterministic over every pinned set, and the five classes are pairwise distinguishable from the report bytes alone.
failsIf: OC-3 is indistinguishable from OC-1 in any pinned report
OC-3 is indistinguishable from OC-2
an UNDETERMINED or CONSENT-REQUIRED check aggregates as success
any exit code or D9 code appears in the fixture as though this contract assigned it
classes.boundedByDr007: This class tests the STRUCTURE only. The value half - which exit each class maps to - cannot be fixtured until DR-007's successor closes, and the class says so rather than pinning a placeholder number. A fixture containing a numeric exit expectation would be this contract inventing what DR-007 owns.

classes.exactByteIntent: A corpus of pinned INPUT bytes, each paired with the pinned doctor report bytes it produces. Tier-1 inputs: a resolved configuration carrying a secret-classified value at a known byte offset; a declared credential environment variable set to a known value; a project at a known absolute path. Tier-2 inputs: a component fault string containing a URL with userinfo, a Bearer token, an inline key=value assignment, an ANSI CSI sequence, a C0 control run, a 10 MB single-line string, and a high-entropy string in NO known credential shape.
classes.passProperty: TIER 1 - the classified secret value's bytes do not occur anywhere in the report bytes, in any encoding, in whole or in any prefix or suffix of length greater than zero; the environment variable's value does not occur while its presence boolean does; no absolute path occurs. TIER 2 - the known-shape credentials are masked; ANSI and control bytes are absent; the long string is truncated with an explicit marker; AND the high-entropy string IS PRESENT UNMASKED, with the report or the contract stating that tier 2 is disclosure, not guarantee.
failsIf: a secret value appears in any form including a first-N-character preview
a hash of a secret value appears in a member usable as an oracle
the high-entropy negative case is quietly masked, which would be the fixture asserting a guarantee the mechanism cannot keep
a tier-2 claim is written as a guarantee anywhere in the report or contract
classes.theNegativeCaseIsTheImportantOne: The high-entropy-unmasked case is the class's centre of gravity. A redaction corpus that only contains cases the scrubber catches proves the scrubber runs; it does not state the bound. This corpus pins the bound by pinning a case that passes through.

classes.exactByteIntent: Four pinned invocations with their report bytes: core mode with no project present; core mode with a project present but core mode requested; project mode with a healthy project; project mode with a project root present but unresolvable.
classes.passProperty: environment.mode and environment.modeSelectionReason are correct in all four; project-scoped checks are NOT-APPLICABLE in core mode and never FAIL; and in the unresolvable case the report is PROJECT mode with UNDETERMINED project checks, never a core-mode report.
failsIf: silent downgrade from project to core mode
a project-scoped check reports FAIL in core mode because the project is absent
core mode fails because no project exists

consent is inferred from a credential's presence or from a declared posture
a prompt is issued in a non-interactive context
a networked-posture target is executed under CA-1/CA-2 alone
a manifest grants its own consent

a residual limitation is null on any consent record
execution is recorded 'enforced' with no measured confinement
recorded bytes or endpoint disagree with the independent observation
a consented action that failed or timed out produced no record

classes.exactByteIntent: Seven pinned broken-input images, one per DEG-1..DEG-7, each byte-pinned pre and post, each with its doctor report bytes: bit-flipped install entries against a recorded inventory; a truncated lock, a duplicate-key lock, and an absent lock; a lock referencing an uninstalled component; an artifact present in the recorded revocation state; a state tree left at each position of the prepare/commit/abort ladder including the post-crash ambiguous case; a fixture whose host clock is skewed forward and backward across the invocation with recorded revocation and expiry timestamps pinned (DEG-6); and a fixture in which a named state source's identity is mutated by a second process between doctor's first and last measurement of it (DEG-7).
classes.passProperty: A report is emitted in every case; DL-1, DL-2 and DL-3 hold in every case; UNDETERMINED and FAIL are used according to whether doctor reached a verdict; the duplicate-key case refuses the document while NAMING the duplicated key; the skew case reports recorded timestamps as primary evidence and marks any age-dependent verdict UNDETERMINED rather than emitting a confident staleness (DEG-6); and the concurrent-mutation case reports UNDETERMINED with cause source-changed-under-observation for every check that consumed the moved source, while checks over stable sources keep their verdicts (DEG-7).

doctor repairs, refreshes, regenerates, or heals anything
doctor answers a different question under the same check id
a duplicate key is resolved last-key-wins
the self-verification scope of DEG-1 is asserted rather than disclosed

doctor acquires a lease, refcount, or lock on any state source in order to obtain read consistency (DEG-7) - detection is the mechanism, acquisition is a mutation-adjacent act the contract forbids
a check keeps a PASS or FAIL verdict that rested on a source whose identity changed under observation (DEG-7)

namedDifferences.prototype: The doctor probe EXECUTES on the default path with no consent of any kind: probeAdapter calls resolveBinary (which may execute `which`/`where` via execFileSync with a 5000 ms timeout) and then probeBinaryVersion (which executes the resolved binary with its versionArgs via execFileSync with a 15000 ms timeout). The subprocess count is PATH-DEPENDENT and is stated here at its measured width: resolveBinary tries env pin, then config pin, then `which`/`where`, first hit wins, and probeBinaryVersion runs only `if (resolution.found)`. TWO subprocesses run for a bare `opensip <tool> doctor` only on the no-pin, found-on-PATH path; with an operator pin set `which` never runs (one subprocess), and where nothing resolves probeBinaryVersion never runs (one subprocess). On every one of those paths the default executes something with no consent, which is the DIFF's substance.
namedDifferences.v2: Executing anything is consent class CA-1 (component) or CA-2 (customer tool). In the default posture no process is spawned and the dependent checks report CONSENT-REQUIRED.
namedDifferences.reason: File 04 makes 'no component code' a DEFAULT and requires 'named consent for component/customer tool execution'. The prototype's default is the exact posture the clause names as requiring consent. The scoping is also not merely a policy toggle: consent carries a scope bound, an expiry, and a mandatory post-report, none of which a module-level timeout constant expresses.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Keep default probing and add a --no-probe opt-out. Rejected: an opt-out inverts the default the clause states, and it makes the safe posture the one the operator must remember. It also cannot produce a post-report for the probe that ran before the operator knew there was one.

namedDifferences.prototype: AdapterDoctorReport is expressly NOT a member of the closed CommandResult union (the source says so), and the command declares output 'raw-stream' with rawStreamReason 'diagnostic-gate' - the host's sanctioned runtime-conditional output escape - because the command-result dispatch arm 'cannot do both shapes'.
namedDifferences.v2: The doctor report IS the host's stable machine schema, inside the host's result model, with one shape from which every projection (human, machine) is rendered.
namedDifferences.reason: The register cell demands a 'stable schema', and file 02 assigns 'host-owned human, JSON, and applicable SARIF projection' to the host while forbidding components to render product UI. A shape that escapes the closed union has no compatibility row, no stability rule, and no reader contract - which is precisely what DR-114 exists to supply.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Preserve the escape and version the escaped shape separately. Rejected: an output mode chosen because the dispatch arm could not carry two shapes is a dispatcher limitation, not a design; carrying it forward would mean the slice's second command is the one command outside the result model.

namedDifferences.prototype: The adapter's doctor handler chooses the process exit itself: `if (!report.ready) { cli.setExitCode(EXIT_CODES.CONFIGURATION_ERROR); }` - a component-supplied handler selecting a fixed numeric exit (2).
namedDifferences.v2: Doctor's report carries an OUTCOME CLASS (OC-1..OC-5) and nothing numeric. The mapping from class to exit is the host's, and its VALUES are DR-007's (ID-DEP-1). No component chooses an exit.
namedDifferences.reason: File 02 is express that components 'must not ... choose verdicts/exits' and requires 'consistent host verdict/finalization/D9/exit mapping'. Independently, DR-007 is HARD-BLOCKED and its blueprint-impact cell forbids V2 defining typed result or exit, so carrying the prototype's value would be inventing what DR-007 owns.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Carry EXIT_CODES.CONFIGURATION_ERROR forward as the not-ready exit, since it exists and works. Rejected twice over: it would let a component-side handler keep exit authority, and it would assign a number this artifact has no authority to assign. The prototype's values are recorded in recordedInputs for the DIFF record only.

namedDifferences.prototype: The report's summary is a single boolean `ready`, computed at the measured digest as `resolution.found && versionStatus !== 'too-old' && (network !== 'auth-required' || (credential?.present ?? false))` - quoted here with the optional chain and the `?? false` default intact, which v1's rendering dropped. There is no per-check structure, no notion of a check that could not be answered, and no residual-limitation member anywhere in AdapterDoctorReport.
namedDifferences.v2: checks[] with a five-token status set in which UNDETERMINED and CONSENT-REQUIRED are non-success and distinguishable from PASS, a required-but-nullable residualLimitation on every check, and no aggregate boolean in the envelope.
namedDifferences.reason: A boolean cannot express 'we could not tell', so every unanswerable condition collapses into false (indistinguishable from a real defect) or into true (a clean bill for something nobody inspected). This is the honesty rule the whole schema is built around, and the register cell's 'stable schema' is unsatisfiable without it.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Keep `ready` as a convenience member alongside the checks. Rejected: a convenience boolean becomes the member every CI script reads, which restores the collapse it was supposed to avoid while adding a second source of truth that can disagree with the checks.

namedDifferences.prototype: TWO unrelated doctor surfaces exist, documented as different by the prototype's own reference: `tools doctor` 'Shows buffered bootstrap diagnostics for the current CLI run ... It is different from an adapter-specific opensip <tool> doctor, which probes that scanner's native binary, version, network posture, and cache prerequisites.' They have different shapes (ToolsDoctorResult vs AdapterDoctorReport), different exit behavior, and no common schema.
namedDifferences.v2: ONE doctor report schema. Component-supplied material - liveness, declared prerequisites, deprecation state - enters as EVIDENCE inside host-written checks, under one envelope, one status set, one outcome derivation.
namedDifferences.reason: The register row says 'Doctor stable machine schema' in the singular, and file 02 requires 'consistent look-and-feel and operability across components' with 'doctor integration' supplied BY the host/SDK contract rather than reimplemented per component. Two schemas mean a reader must know which doctor produced a report before it can parse it.

Rejected: the split is a discovery, not a design - it arose because bootstrap diagnostics and adapter probes were built at different times for different questions. Both questions are checks; the class member (COMPONENT-INVENTORY versus COMPONENT-LIVENESS) carries the distinction without a second schema.

namedDifferences.v2: No-network is DOCTOR's default property (DP-3), and egress is consent class CA-4. Where a consented execution's target declares a network posture, a separate CA-4 consent is REQUIRED or the action is refused (consentDoesNotCascade).

The prototype's declaration-only posture is honest but is a statement about the TARGET; doctor's default must be a statement about DOCTOR, which is enforceable because doctor controls its own sockets.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Treat a local-only declared posture as sufficient to permit execution with no egress consent, since the declaration exists. Rejected: the declaration is unenforced by the prototype's own record, so relying on it would convert an honest label into a guarantee. Instead the local-only case executes under CA-1/CA-2 alone with the unenforced-ness recorded as a residual limitation, and the networked case refuses.

namedDifferences.prototype: The credential environment variable name is MINTED by string template from the tool name: `OPENSIP_${tool.replaceAll('-','_').toUpperCase()}_TOKEN`. The same pattern appears for the binary override (defaultBinaryEnvVar).
namedDifferences.v2: The credential environment variable name is a DECLARED manifest field. Doctor reports presence for declared names only and never constructs a name to look up.

namedDifferences.prototype: redactSecret returns a PREVIEW: the first 4 characters plus an ellipsis for values longer than 4, and '…' for values of length <= 4. secretHash returns the first 12 hex characters of the value's sha256.
namedDifferences.v2: The doctor report carries no secret preview and no secret-derived hash. Handle plus presence boolean only.
namedDifferences.reason: A 4-character prefix is 4 characters of a live credential, and for structured credentials the prefix is the discriminating part (a key-type prefix identifies the issuer and often the account class). A truncated hash is an oracle: an attacker holding a candidate can confirm it. Neither is needed by any doctor check, because no doctor check must tell two secrets apart - which is the exact need that justifies both functions in their prototype context.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Carry secretHash for evidence identity, so two invocations can be compared. Rejected: doctor mints no identity at all (ID-DEP-10), and comparing invocations is not a doctor obligation. The need does not exist, so the oracle has no justification.

namedDifferences.prototype: The honest bound on pattern-based redaction exists as a SOURCE COMMENT: 'Conservative by design — it targets known credential shapes, not arbitrary high-entropy strings.' There is no structural distinction in the code or the emitted data between values whose redaction is guaranteed by construction and free text that was merely scrubbed.
namedDifferences.v2: A structural TWO-TIER split: tier 1 (host-constructed members over classified sources) carries a GUARANTEE enforceable by the construction path; tier 2 (free text) carries a DISCLOSURE. Every report member is classified into exactly one tier, and FC-REDACT pins a high-entropy negative case that passes through unmasked.
namedDifferences.reason: The corpus's honesty discipline requires that an unenforceable redaction claim be stated as disclosure, not guarantee. A source comment is not a claim a report's reader can see; a reader of a scrubbed report cannot tell whether a member is guaranteed clean or merely pattern-checked, and will assume the stronger reading.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: State one guarantee over all report strings and back it with an entropy heuristic. Rejected: entropy heuristics produce false negatives (low-entropy passphrases) and false positives (legitimate digests destroyed), and a guarantee that fails on unanticipated input is exactly the claim the corpus requires be downgraded to disclosure. The bound is the claim.

namedDifferences.prototype: AdapterDoctorReport emits `binary.path` - the resolved ABSOLUTE filesystem path of the tool - and `binary.layer`, unredacted, into both the human lines and the `--json` output. The host's own projectRelativePath discipline exists in packages/core/src/lib/safe-diagnostic-data.ts but is not applied on this path. That function is THREE-branch at the measured digest, stated here at full width because v1 described only two: with a projectRoot it returns the project-relative form for paths under the root and the literal '[absolute-path]' for anything outside it; with NO projectRoot it returns `scrubText(filePath, 512)` - the full absolute path, scrubbed and length-bounded, collapsing nothing. The third branch is precisely the core-mode case, where by definition no project root exists.
namedDifferences.v2: Paths in the doctor report are redaction-classified: project-relative inside the project root, a non-identifying marker outside it. environment.expresslyExcluded names absolute install paths, home directories, and usernames.
namedDifferences.reason: An absolute path outside the project discloses the operator's account name, home layout, and installation topology to whoever reads the report - and doctor reports are exactly what operators paste into issue trackers and support channels. The prototype already HAS the correct discipline; the DIFF is that the doctor path does not use it.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Keep the absolute path because an operator debugging a resolution problem needs it. Rejected in favour of the resolution LAYER plus a redacted path form: the layer ('operator pin via config', 'operator pin via env', 'declared closure') answers the debugging question, and where the literal path is genuinely needed it is an operator-only projection decision, not a default report member.

namedDifferences.prototype: Neither doctor surface carries a schema version, an environment block, a mode indicator, or any stability rule. ToolsDoctorResult is three members (type, diagnostics, totalCount); AdapterDoctorReport is seven. A reader has no way to detect a shape change other than by breaking. Both of ToolsDoctorResult's non-payload members are named here rather than absorbed silently: `totalCount`, a derived aggregate over the diagnostics array, and `type`, the closed-union discriminant.
namedDifferences.v2: Required envelope members schemaVersion, mode, outcome, environment, checks, consentRecords, residualLimitations; explicit additive-versus-never-change stability rules; refusal rather than best-effort parse on an unsupported major; and a proposed DR-111 compatibility row. The two ToolsDoctorResult members named above have no envelope counterpart, deliberately: `totalCount` is not carried because every aggregate a reader needs is derivable from `checks` whose statuses are individually present, and a derived count that can drift from the array it counts is a second source of truth - the envelope's rule is that it carries no aggregate BOOLEAN (whatIsNotInTheEnvelope, DIFF-4) and this contract additionally carries no aggregate COUNT; `type` is subsumed by the host result model the doctor report enters under DIFF-2, where the shape is discriminated by the result model rather than by a member of its own. Neither omission carries an honesty hazard, unlike the `ready` boolean DIFF-4 rejects, but both are named rather than left as unnamed divergence.
namedDifferences.reason: 'Stable schema' in the register cell is a statement about READERS over time, which requires a version the reader can check and a rule about what may change under it. Without them the schema is merely a current shape.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Version implicitly by the core release version. Rejected by file 04 directly: 'There is no shared N/N-1/N-2 promise and no common version number.' Borrowing the core's version is the coupling the separate-matrices section exists to forbid.

namedDifferences.prototype: probeBinaryVersion swallows every failure and returns `undefined`, with the source recording the intent: 'a version probe failure (binary missing, slow, or a non-version output) is a normal "version unknown" — surfaced as undefined, which doctor renders.' compareVersion then maps undefined to VersionStatus 'unknown', and `ready` does not require a known version - a probe that timed out and a probe whose tool printed an unparseable banner are indistinguishable, and neither prevents ready:true.
namedDifferences.v2: A check that could not reach a verdict reports UNDETERMINED with a NON-NULL residual limitation naming the cause (input-unreadable, dependency-absent, observation-bounded), and UNDETERMINED is not success-bearing. The distinct failure reasons are distinct evidence.
namedDifferences.reason: 'Unknown' collapsing into 'ready' is the specific shape of the failure this contract's honesty rule exists to prevent: a timed-out probe becomes a passing doctor. Distinguishing why a verdict was not reached is also what makes the report actionable rather than merely accurate.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Keep the silent-undefined seam and add a warning line. Rejected: a warning that does not change the check's status does not change what CI does, and the source's own note ('No logger is available in this pure seam') shows the seam was chosen for testability rather than semantics. The residual-limitation member is the structural place that information belongs.

namedDifferences.prototype: Ambient PATH lookup is a first-class RESOLUTION LAYER: resolveBinary tries the env pin, then the config pin, then the system PATH via `which`/`where`. The design is careful (a non-absolute or missing pin is a hard miss with no silent PATH fallback; 'resolution NEVER fetches a binary'), but PATH remains a supported source of the executable doctor then runs.
namedDifferences.v2: Doctor performs NO ambient resolution of any kind: no PATH, no loader search, no system-runtime lookup. A component's tooling comes from its signed closure; the only PATH-shaped case is the DR-119/D-008 customer-owned external system, identified from its manifest DECLARATION and executed only under CA-2 consent.
namedDifferences.reason: File 04's exact-byte-delivery section (lines 152-153) states as a prohibition bullet: 'no `PATH`, loader, shell, live-project, system-runtime, or install-time substitution; and', in a list whose preceding bullet requires 'entrypoint and runtime-library resolution inside that tree' (line 151); and DR-119/D-008 forbids 'ambient PATH/system-runtime lookup, project package-manager resolution, or implicit download' for language tooling, with D-008 ACCEPTED universally. (v1 rendered the file 04 bullet as "forbids 'no PATH, loader, ...'", keeping the source's leading 'no' inside a 'forbids' frame - a double negative that reads as forbidding the ABSENCE of PATH substitution. The bullet is quoted here as the source's own prohibition bullet, with its leading 'no' intact and no 'forbids' frame wrapped around it.) A diagnostic that resolves through PATH reports on a binary the analysis path would refuse to run, which is DL-3's silent-different-question failure in its most damaging form.
namedDifferences.alternativeRejected: Retain PATH as a last-resort layer so doctor can tell the operator that a tool exists somewhere on the system. Rejected: that is a helpfulness that reports on the wrong artifact. Where a tool is absent from the closure, the honest report is that the closure lacks it, with a PREREQUISITE-ABSENT remediation naming the operator action - not a note that a differently-provenanced binary was found elsewhere.

carriedForward: CliDiagnostic's shape and its closed 16-member CLI_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES set (count re-measured at the recorded digest in this authoring session; v1 recited 17, which did not replicate): a structured diagnostic with severity, stable machine code, category, message, IMPACT (what the failure means for the run) and optional ACTION (remediation hint) is the strongest thing in the prototype's diagnostic layer, and the check object's title/evidence/residualLimitation/remediation shape is its descendant. The impact-and-action pairing in particular is carried, not reinvented. Nothing in this design depends on the cardinality; the number is corrected because a recited count that does not replicate is a defect under freeze 7.2.2 even where the conclusion survives.
Deny-by-default for Error and cause objects (toSafeDiagnosticData returns name + scrubbed message + an explicit redaction marker rather than the object).
ANSI-then-control ordering in text neutralization, which exists because ESC is itself a control code.
String length bounding with an explicit truncation marker.

projectRelativePath's discipline of projecting inside-root paths to relative form and collapsing outside-root paths to a non-identifying marker (carried, and now applied on the doctor path - see DIFF-10).
The single subprocess/IO boundary with descriptor-controlled argument vectors and no shell strings.
Presence-only reporting for credentials (never the value) - carried in full; only the NAME's provenance changes (DIFF-7).
Deterministic layered resolution with a hard miss on a bad operator pin and no silent fallback - carried, minus the PATH layer (DIFF-13).

classes.verdict: SPLIT - a host-actor head and a genuinely component-actor tail.
classes.hostActorHalf: THE DECISION TO SPAWN, and the whole of the in-process variant. Doctor decides to execute, doctor calls exec, and doctor does so because the operator named CA-1 at the invocation. No component asked; the host acted on direct instruction, which is DR-105's fourth non-token exactly. The in-process half is worse than unowned: CA-1 covers 'running component code in-process', and DR-105 mints no token for loading component code into the host address space at all - it treats in-host-process as a TABLE AXIS, not a grantable act (the review's GAP-1). If V2 admits the in-host mode, CA-1's realised form is the half with no token in principle.
classes.componentActorHalf: EVERYTHING THE SPAWNED COMPONENT THEN DOES. Once the component process is running, its reads, its writes and its egress are its own acts, declared in its own admitted manifest, and PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE and PT-NET-EGRESS are squarely the right tokens held by squarely the right actor. This contract already draws that exact line for a different reason: consentDoesNotCascade states that 'consent to execute something is never consent for what that thing then does'. The line the cascade rule draws and the line the actor question draws are the same line.
classes.couldRideDr105Today: The tail, yes - and it does not need this contract's help to, because the component's manifest is its authorization record. The head, no.
joinFindingsThisExplains: TERM-6 (CA-1 is irreversible by DR-105's own byToken ruling)

classes.name: customer tool execution
classes.verdict: HOST-ACTOR ENTIRELY. No component-actor half exists.
classes.analysis: A customer-owned external tool is not an admitted component. It has no admitted manifest, no permissions[] block, and no admitted immutable tree - so there is no artifact anywhere in which DR-105's REQUESTED declaration could be made, by anyone. The actor is doctor, executing a program that belongs to neither OpenSIP nor any admitted component, because the operator named CA-2. DR-105 independently closes the same door from its own side: PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED is bounded to a program 'from inside the component's own admitted immutable tree', which a customer-owned tool is by definition not, and its own sliceJustification says that bound 'is what keeps it from becoming a general execute-anything grant'; separately its reserved point for third-party execution reads EXCLUDED, not reserved-for-this-lane, with minting assigned elsewhere and explicitly 'not this contract'.
classes.couldRideDr105Today: No, on two independent grounds - wrong actor, and an effect DR-105 states it will never mint. Neither ground is a cardinality question.
classes.productConsequenceIfHostSurfacesAreSubje: CA-2 becomes UNEXERCISABLE under this contract's own fail-closed rule, and DR-119/D-008's customer-owned external-system exception - ACCEPTED, and required by file 02 to appear 'in manifest and doctor output' with typed absence/failure behavior - loses its doctor carrier. This contract supplies that carrier at check class PLATFORM-PREREQUISITE and remediation class PREREQUISITE-ABSENT (ID-DEP-9), and would be shipping a doctor that must report CONSENT-REQUIRED for a requirement the corpus has already accepted. Recorded as a consequence for the decider, not as an argument for an option.

classes.name: probes
classes.verdict: HOST-ACTOR ENTIRELY, and the purest case of the four.
classes.analysis: Every one of CA-3's four covered effects - stat-ing or reading a path outside the install and project roots, opening a local socket or named pipe, reading an OS keychain entry, querying a privileged platform facility - is performed BY DOCTOR, IN DOCTOR'S OWN PROCESS. No component is involved in any of them at any point, so there is no manifest that could declare any of them even in principle. DR-105's vocabulary independently has no token for any of the four: an out-of-root read is not covered by PT-FS-READ-PROJECT (bounded inside the project root, with symlinks resolved before the containment test) or by PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT (bounded to the component's own tree), and is not even a reserved extension point; local socket and IPC endpoints are RESERVED, not minted; keychain is RESERVED, not minted, with D-002 having deferred DR-108 out of slice 1 entirely; and a privileged platform facility is not enumerated anywhere, leaving it undecidable whether it is reserved or absent.
classes.couldRideDr105Today: No, on every branch, on both grounds - wrong actor AND no token.

classes.name: egress
classes.verdict: SPLIT - doctor's own egress is host-actor; a spawned component's egress is component-actor and already joins cleanly.
classes.hostActorHalf: DOCTOR'S OWN SOCKET. CA-4's own definition is 'any network send or receive by doctor', and DIFF-6 states the ground of the whole no-network default: doctor's default 'must be a statement about DOCTOR, which is enforceable because doctor controls its own sockets.' PT-NET-EGRESS is a component's token, declared in a component's manifest; doctor has neither. The mismatch has a measurable edge here that runs the OTHER way from every other finding: if CA-4 were forced onto PT-NET-EGRESS, DR-105's DISCLOSED obligation for that row would oblige the host to disclose that the actor is trusted code in the TCB and that the grant record is a record of asking rather than of confinement - which, applied to doctor's own egress, is FALSE, because doctor does control its own sockets. The join would force a mandatory UNDER-claim over a genuinely enforced act. Recorded as a measured consequence; it argues for no option here.
classes.componentActorHalf: EGRESS BY A COMPONENT OR TOOL DOCTOR SPAWNED UNDER CA-1 OR CA-2. That egress is the component's own act under its own manifest, PT-NET-EGRESS is exactly the right token held by exactly the right actor, and this is the one place the pair already agrees end to end: this contract REFUSES a CA-1/CA-2 execution against a target whose declared posture includes network unless CA-4 is separately named (consentDoesNotCascade.theHardCase), and DR-105 reaches the same answer from the other end - PT-NET-EGRESS denied by absence, and DISCLOSURE-ONLY in all four of its cells, so no mechanism would have contained the spawned process. Two lanes authored blind reached the same posture.
classes.couldRideDr105Today: The component half, yes, and it is the pair's one clean join. Doctor's own egress, no.

summary.genuinelyComponentActorAndAbleToRideDr10: CA-1's tail (the spawned component's own subsequent effects) and CA-4's derivative case (egress by a component or tool doctor spawned under CA-1/CA-2). In both, the actor is genuinely the component, its admitted manifest is genuinely the authorization record, and DR-105's tokens fit without strain.
summary.hostActorAndWithoutAnOwner: CA-1's head (the decision to spawn) and the whole of CA-1's in-process variant; CA-2 entirely; CA-3 entirely, on all four of its covered effects; and CA-4's primary case, doctor's own socket.
summary.countedPlainly: Of the four classes, ZERO are wholly component-actor, TWO are wholly host-actor (CA-2, CA-3), and TWO split (CA-1, CA-4). The component-actor material that exists is real and joins cleanly, but in both cases it is the CONSEQUENCE of a doctor action rather than the doctor action itself - which is why the join looked closeable from a distance and does not close up close.

theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.why: The actor question does not begin at the consent classes. Doctor's UNCONSENTED default posture already performs effects DR-105's tables would classify as permissioned: core and project mode read the installed generation inventory, core-owned state, other components' index custody records and admitted manifest metadata, the project's strict configuration and lock, and the allowlisted environment layer; and doctor writes its own audit record inside the Operational metadata class.
theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.effectDescriptionsThatMatch: PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-ENV-READ and PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE describe those effects. They are NAMED here as effect descriptions that match, and expressly NOT as permissions this contract holds, requests, or claims - naming a token is not carrying one, and this artifact contains zero permission tokens by measurement.
theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.andTwoOfThemDoNotFitEvenAsWritten: Two of the four cannot express a host surface's act at all, on their own wording: PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is scoped to the host-owned state namespace 'allocated to this component for its declared state class', and doctor's audit record is allocated to no component; PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT is bounded to 'the component's own immutable installed tree', and doctor reads OTHER components' trees and index records. This is simultaneously a miss on doctor's side and a coverage hole on DR-105's, and neither artifact could have seen it alone.
theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.andOneCannotBeEnforcedForAHostAtAll: PT-ENV-READ is the ONLY token in the whole 28-cell table carrying ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION (2 of 28 cells, one per platform; the only other enforced cells are PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED's two ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER), and its named mechanism is the envp argument to execve(2) / the environment array passed to posix_spawn(3) - a mechanism a PARENT operates on a CHILD. Doctor is the parent. Nobody constructs doctor's environment block. The single structurally enforced mechanism in the pair is un-instantiable for a host surface, which is a property of the actor relation rather than of any wording.
theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.theConsequenceForTheDefault: If host surfaces are subject to the vocabulary, doctor's default posture is a fully permissioned action set that doctor gates with nothing, and under closure it is denied. This contract does not gate its default posture and does not propose to: the four default properties are asserted as PROPERTIES of a host surface, not as permissions it was granted. Whether that framing survives is the routed decision.
theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo.oneRuleThatHoldsEitherWay: Should the decision subject doctor to the vocabulary, a denial of any default read does NOT silently reduce doctor's coverage. This contract's no-silent-downgrade rule governs the case unchanged: doctor stays in the mode the invocation selected, reports every check it could not reach as UNDETERMINED with a residual limitation naming the denial, and never answers an easier question under the same check id (DL-3). A project-read denial that quietly turned project mode into a clean core-mode report is the exact silent degradation both artifacts independently forbid, and this rule is stated here so it is not left to fall out.

hostActorAuthorizationIsUnowned.form: Recorded in the UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED form the component-manifest candidate used for the configuration classification vocabulary at its ID-DEP-12 - the corpus's existing idiom for a surface that is needed, that no register row mints, and that the artifact needing it must not mint for itself.
hostActorAuthorizationIsUnowned.statement: THE AUTHORIZATION ORIGIN FOR A HOST SURFACE ACTING UNDER THE INVOKING USER'S DIRECT INSTRUCTION IS UNOWNED-AND-NEEDED. NO register row mints it. DR-105 owns COMPONENT permission vocabulary and expressly rules one host-actor case OUT of that vocabulary without naming what governs host actors instead. DR-G09 owns the truthfulness of requested/granted/denied and enforced/disclosed outcomes, but over the same component-shaped grant harness. File 03 supplies the laws that hold regardless - deny wins, absence denies, authority is not self-granted, required confinement refuses when unenforceable, CI never prompts - and supplies no origin. This row records the gap as UNOWNED rather than pretending an owner exists, and mints nothing to fill it: minting a host-actor permission vocabulary here would be a diagnostic surface creating the authority under which it acts, which is the self-granted authority file 03 forbids components, exercised by a host contract instead.
hostActorAuthorizationIsUnowned.whatIsDecidableWithoutIt: Everything this contract binds that does not depend on an authorization origin: the two modes and the non-admission line, the report schema and its stability rules, the redaction guarantee and its bound, the outcome-class structure, the degraded and hostile input behavior, the remediation record's shape, and - within the consent model - who may name a consent, how, what it binds, and what must be reported afterwards. What is UNDECIDABLE until an owner exists is by what authority a host surface asks at all, and therefore whether doctor's consent record is a DR-105 grant or a doctor-side record with its own lifecycle.
hostActorAuthorizationIsUnowned.whatMustNotBeInferredFromThisGap: That doctor's consented actions are therefore unpermissioned, or permitted by default. This contract's fail-closed rule is unconditional and survives every option below: an action class with no resolved authorization is UNEXERCISABLE and its dependent checks report CONSENT-REQUIRED. A gap in ownership never widens what doctor may do.

routedToACoordinatorDecision.whyItMustBeDecidedBeforeEitherRowCloses: Applying DR-105 alone is coherent, and applying DR-114 alone is coherent - this contract's permissionRef stays reserved and its default posture is complete with no token at all. Applying BOTH activates the mismatch and every consequence enumerated above at once, and neither artifact contains disposition text that resolves it.

candidateResolutions.statedNeutrally: WIDEN DR-105 WITH A SECOND ACTOR CLASS. The vocabulary acquires host-actor permissions alongside component permissions, with an authorization origin defined for a host acting on the operator's direct instruction, and the truth tables gain the corresponding rows or a second axis.
candidateResolutions.costs: Requires a DR-105 successor: the current candidate's vocabulary is CLOSED at seven tokens and its fourth deliberate non-token rules the host-under-direct-instruction case OUT on a stated principle, so this option reverses a position that artifact took deliberately and must say why. routedToACoordinatorDecision.noRecommendationIsMade: This artifact expresses NO preference among A, B and C, and nothing in the ordering, the length, or the phrasing above should be read as one. The costs are recorded because a decider needs them, not to weight them.
